title: Ripple CEO Says Crypto Is Here to Stay as Pro-Crypto Lawmakers Win
summary: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse cited 67 million American crypto users as he highlighted bipartisan election victories. His comments reinforced the company’s push to keep digital asset development in the United States under clearer rules. Garlinghouse Points to Crypto’s Staying Power Ripple CEO Brad Ga...
content:
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse cited 67 million American crypto users as he highlighted bipartisan election victories. His comments reinforced the company’s push to keep digital asset development in the United States under clearer rules.

Key Takeaways

  • Garlinghouse highlighted pro-crypto election wins across both parties.
  • He cited 67 million American crypto users as a growing constituency.
  • The Ripple CEO called for clear rules and crypto development in America.

Garlinghouse Points to Crypto’s Staying Power

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said on Nov. 4 that pro-crypto candidates had won across party lines in the U.S. elections. The message on X accompanied a statement from Ripple Chief Legal Officer Stuart Alderoty on the industry’s political position.

In his assessment of bipartisan crypto support, Garlinghouse stated:

“Pro-crypto members won on both sides of the aisle … and the 67M (and growing) Americans using crypto aren’t going anywhere. New Congress, with the same mission: clear rules, built in America.”

The 67 million crypto ownership estimate appeared in the National Cryptocurrency Association’s 2026 State of Crypto Holders Report, released May 13. The crypto education nonprofit, whose president is Alderoty, produced the research with The Harris Poll, a polling and market research firm. Its findings put ownership at roughly one in four American adults, up from one in five a year earlier.

Fairshake Wins Reflect Years of Political Engagement

Alderoty credited Fairshake, a super PAC supporting pro-crypto candidates, with meaningful victories in both primaries and the general election. Super PACs are political action committees that can raise unlimited funds for election spending independent of candidates’ campaigns. In his statement on crypto’s election results, the Ripple legal chief attributed the industry’s position to years of work by grassroots advocates and industry organizations.

Stand With Crypto, a crypto advocacy organization, maintains congressional candidate ratings that track politicians’ positions on digital assets. Alderoty stated: “Early Stand With Crypto data shows a substantial number of pro-crypto members elected across both parties.”

Company funding formed another part of that effort well before this election. Ripple disclosed its third $25 million Fairshake contribution in November 2024, extending its financial support for the group’s work. At the time, Alderoty described the contribution as part of Ripple’s pledge to remain a strong force in Washington for years to come.

Policy Work Extends Beyond a Single Election Cycle

Earlier this year, Alderoty pursued outreach to undecided Senate offices as lawmakers considered the CLARITY Act. In September, he urged senators to meet Americans who held crypto before voting. His approach brought constituents’ experiences into discussions about federal digital asset legislation.

After the measure failed to advance in the Senate, his call for coordinated industry advocacy focused on improving the industry’s policy message. Following the election, Alderoty wrote:

“Congratulations to everyone elected this week. We look forward to working with members of both parties to keep America the best place in the world to build the future.”

“Clear rules for digital assets were never a one-cycle project,” he added.

Beyond electoral politics, Alderoty described crypto use in everyday finance as mainstream finance, pointing to adoption by banks and businesses. He said Americans used digital assets to build financial independence, power businesses, and pay for goods and services. Ripple’s planned work included political engagement through super PACs and other advocacy groups, plus education through nonprofits such as the National Cryptocurrency Association.

title: XRP Tradable Supply on Binance Tightens as Scarcity Hits Four-Year High
summary: XRP’s tradable supply on Binance tightened as a scarcity gauge reached its highest reading since 2022, according to a new analysis. Separate reserve data showed rising exchange holdings, highlighting the distinction between trading availability and total balances. XRP Scarcity Gauge Reaches Highest ...
content:
XRP’s tradable supply on Binance tightened as a scarcity gauge reached its highest reading since 2022, according to a new analysis. Separate reserve data showed rising exchange holdings, highlighting the distinction between trading availability and total balances.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance’s XRP scarcity gauge climbed to approximately 2.1.
  • Binance’s total reserves rose by 280 million XRP in two days.
  • Demand and trading liquidity remained central to the price outlook.

XRP Scarcity Gauge Reaches Highest Reading Since 2022

The XRP Binance Scarcity Index reached approximately 2.1, its highest level since 2022, Cryptoquant contributor Arab Chain shared in a Nov. 5 analysis. The gauge measures relative XRP availability for trading on Binance, with higher readings indicating greater scarcity. Its latest level followed negative readings throughout September and October and marked its highest point since 2022.

Earlier fluctuations included sharp declines during 2023 and 2024, followed by improvements through parts of 2025 and 2026. The analyst stated:

“This development points to a decline in the amount of XRP available for trading on Binance, reflecting a relative reduction in circulating exchange supply and an increase in scarcity.”

Price implications depended on demand, buying activity, and liquidity movements, the analysis explained. A sustained reduction in available tokens could influence the exchange’s supply-and-demand balance if buying strengthened. The analyst added: “If this trend continues, it could limit the amount of XRP available to traders on the platform.”

Binance Reserves Rose Alongside the Scarcity Signal

Cryptoquant contributor Amr Taha placed Binance’s XRP reserves at 2.63 billion on Nov. 5, up from 2.35 billion on Nov. 3. The 280 million XRP increase measured total exchange holdings, a separate metric from the scarcity index.

Trading conditions also depend on order-book depth and spreads. Depth measures the amount of buy and sell orders available at different prices, showing how much trading a market can absorb. A shallow order book can experience sharp price movements when a large order arrives.

More broadly, market liquidity reflects how easily assets can be exchanged without substantial price changes. Orders close to the current price help traders execute larger transactions with less disruption. Those conditions provide a practical measure of trading availability alongside exchange balance data.

Reserve Trends and Large-Holder Activity Add Context

Historical reserve data captured a longer period: Cryptoquant contributor Darkfost’s Sept. 1 assessment put Binance’s monthly average XRP reserves near 2.6 billion, versus 3.1 billion in November 2025. This roughly 500 million XRP decrease accumulated across that interval. Using a monthly average smoothed shorter-term fluctuations.

Large-holder transfers offered a different perspective, with Arab Chain tracking 1.38 billion XRP in whale withdrawals over 30 days in an Oct. 7 analysis. Whale withdrawals are transfers off an exchange by large holders. The gross total excluded deposits, so it differed from the net change in reserves.

Beyond exchange flows, Santiment counted 2,147 wallets holding at least 1 million XRP on Nov. 3, the year’s highest tally. That measure tracked addresses crossing a balance threshold, distinct from purchase volume. The category expanded by 28 wallets over 10 days, including 18 during the final three.

title: Michael Saylor Flags Sharp Market Selloff as Nasdaq Crashes 5.5%
summary: Michael Saylor compared a sharp equity sell-off and bitcoin’s retreat with Strategy’s preferred stock trading near par. His assessment followed the company’s shift to daily dividends and the shares’ return to their $100 benchmark. Saylor Compares Equity Losses With STRC’s Closing Price Michael Saylo...
content:
Michael Saylor compared a sharp equity sell-off and bitcoin’s retreat with Strategy’s preferred stock trading near par. His assessment followed the company’s shift to daily dividends and the shares’ return to their $100 benchmark.

Key Takeaways

  • The Nasdaq fell 5.52%, closing at 24,315 on Nov. 5.
  • Saylor said bitcoin fell about 5% as the S&P 500 dropped 4.4%.
  • STRC closed at $99.56, following its return to $100 a day earlier.

Saylor Compares Equity Losses With STRC’s Closing Price

Michael Saylor, founder and executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (Nasdaq: MSTR), compared equity and bitcoin losses with the company’s STRC preferred stock on Nov. 5. In his market comparison on X, he stated:

“Today was a 4σ day for equities. The S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq fell 5.5%, a decline seen roughly once every 19 months. Bitcoin fell about 5%. $STRC closed at $99.56, just 44 cents below par.”

The Nasdaq Composite finished at 24,315, down 1,421.52 points, or 5.52%, from its previous close of 25,736.52.

Sigma denotes standard deviation, a measure of market volatility that describes how widely daily returns vary around their average. A four-sigma decline describes a daily return four standard deviations below its historical average. How frequently such moves occur depends on the return distribution and historical period used.

Bitcoin had fallen below $77,000 earlier Thursday as technology shares weakened, reversing its post-election recovery. It dropped from Wednesday’s $81,105 peak to $76,059, a decline of approximately 6.22%.

STRC Trades Near Par After Daily Dividend Shift

STRC’s $99.56 finish placed it 0.44% below its $100 stated amount. The shares had reached $100 on Nov. 4, their first return to that level since May, following months of repurchases and a change in dividend payments.

Strategy’s variable-rate preferred stock carries a 12% annualized dividend rate based on the $100 stated amount. The company adjusts the rate monthly to encourage trading around par. Payments are not guaranteed, and the preferred shares are not collateralized by its bitcoin holdings.

Daily dividend accrual began Nov. 1, with the first cash distributions starting Nov. 2 following shareholder approval on Oct. 28. Shareholders accrue dividends on weekends and holidays, while payments generally follow on business days. The change replaced STRC’s twice-monthly distribution schedule.

Trading above $100 could allow Strategy to sell additional STRC shares through its at-the-market offering program, potentially raising capital for further bitcoin purchases. The company has used repurchases to support the stock below that threshold, with year-to-date buybacks reaching approximately $2.04 billion, including unsettled transactions, by Oct. 25. New issuance and bitcoin acquisitions would depend on management decisions and market conditions.

The comparison followed Strategy’s record third-quarter operating income of $20.91 billion, announced Oct. 29 and driven by digital asset valuation gains. Net income totaled $19.53 billion, while revenue declined 3% to $125.4 million. U.S. dollar assets stood at $5.07 billion as of Oct. 25, providing an estimated 3.4 years of coverage for preferred dividends and interest obligations at the time.

Saylor had also predicted that a new bitcoin bull market was beginning in Strategy’s Oct. 29 earnings announcement. He cited growing adoption by banks, renewed institutional demand, and bitcoin trading 21% above its 200-week moving average.

title: Core Scientific to quit Bitcoin mining by year-end as AI business surges
summary: The former Bitcoin mining heavyweight plans to become a pure-play data center provider in 2027, with mining now accounting for just 7.5% of quarterly revenue.
content:
Core Scientific said it expects to exit Bitcoin mining by the end of 2026 as it shifts its business toward artificial intelligence and high-performance computing infrastructure. 

“We expect to complete the wind-down during the fourth quarter and enter 2027 as a pure-play, high-density colocation provider,” said Core Scientific chief financial officer Jim Nygaard during a Q3 earnings call on Thursday. 

Core Scientific had previously disclosed in a July quarterly filing that hosted mining would end by Dec. 31 as it continued to wind down its self-mining operations. The comment establishes a targeted completion date for its complete Bitcoin mining exit. 

Its latest quarterly results show how far the business has shifted. Third-quarter self-mining revenue fell to $12.3 million from $57.4 million a year earlier, while revenue from hosting other miners dropped to $5.2 million from $8.7 million. 

Bitcoin mining generated just $17.5 million, or 7.5%, of Core Scientific’s $232.9 million in third-quarter revenue, compared with $215.4 million from colocation services. 

The company had nearly 50% fewer miners online at the end of September than at the end of 2025, according to Nygaard. 

Core Scientific pivot to AI

Core Scientific’s move into AI hosting took shape in 2024 after signing an initial hosting agreement with CoreWeave in March that year, followed by a much larger deal announced in June.

At the time, Core Scientific presented AI hosting as an expansion alongside its mining business. Its June 2024 announcement emphasized preserving Bitcoin mining capacity.

By December 2025, The Wall Street Journal reported that Core Scientific was already targeting to wind down its Bitcoin mining operations by 2028. 

Related: American Bitcoin’s $126M profit masks mining pressure as rivals turn to AI

Mining economics added pressure in the months following. 

Core Scientific recorded $266.5 million in mining-related asset impairments in the first quarter of 2026, citing weaker Bitcoin prices, historically low hashprice and falling digital asset mining equipment values in the secondary market. 

During the second quarter, it terminated its mining equipment agreement with Block and Proto, recording a $41.9 million loss as part of the transition.

US midterms bring scrutiny of data-center growth

The planned exit comes as the US election results introduce fresh uncertainty for companies expanding AI infrastructure.

Opponents of data-center development were among the winners of the Democrats’ sweeping midterm gains, Reuters reported Wednesday.

The backlash centers partly on electricity bills and the demands large facilities place on local resources.

Cointelegraph reached out to Core Scientific for comment.

title: Elon Musk Jokes About ‘Election-Interfering Space Lasers’ as Polymarket Whale Scores on Texas
summary: A Polymarket user who goes by the name Domer made about $62,700 betting against a Republican win in Texas’ Senate race and mocked the roughly $250 million that Elon Musk-backed groups spent trying to keep the seat Republican, calling it the stupidest thing anyone could do. Musk, posting separately, ...
content:
A Polymarket user who goes by the name Domer made about $62,700 betting against a Republican win in Texas’ Senate race and mocked the roughly $250 million that Elon Musk-backed groups spent trying to keep the seat Republican, calling it the stupidest thing anyone could do. Musk, posting separately, joked that his “election-interfering space lasers” had failed.

Key Takeaways

  • Domer, who trades as ImJustKen, made $62,715 betting against a Republican win in Texas’ Senate race.
  • He spent about $185,900 on the bet, buying “No” shares at an average of 74.6 cents from Nov. 2.
  • Polymarket priced a Republican win at 25.5% on Election Day; Democrat James Talarico beat Ken Paxton.

Domer’s $185,900 Bet Against The Pro-Paxton Millions

A Polymarket account trading as ImJustKen, which is linked to the X account of well-known political bettor Domer, made $62,715 when Polymarket’s Texas Senate market resolved against the Republicans, according to the platform’s data. The account bought 249,215 “No” shares on a Republican win at an average of 74.6 cents, about $185,900 in all, starting Nov. 2.

Polymarket resolved the market at 07:11 UTC on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race. Talarico will replace Republican Sen. John Cornyn, who lost to Paxton in the primary runoff.

Domer, whose X bio describes them as “full-time political bettor since 2007,” has made about $2.33 million in profit on Polymarket across roughly $500.9 million in trading volume, ranking 65th on the platform’s all-time profit board.

Domer Mocks Musk’s Texas Spending

Hours after polls closed, Domer took aim at Musk on X, writing, “A lot of us will do stupid things over the course of our lives. But none of us who will ever do anything stupider than [Musk] spending $250m to try to flip a SAFE BLUE D+12 Senate seat. Lmao.”

The “safe blue” label was sarcasm: Texas had not elected a Democratic senator since 1988, and securing statewide office there has long been a mirage for the party.

Three Musk-funded committees spent $249.2 million supporting Paxton or attacking Talarico, Benzinga reported, citing a Black Mesa analysis of federal filings that includes money from other donors as well as Musk’s. The Associated Press put Talarico’s margin at about 12 points with most votes counted.

Outside groups backing Paxton spent almost three times as much as those supporting Talarico, and Talarico made Musk’s involvement a campaign issue. Verasight CEO Ben Leff had told Benzinga before the vote that spending had limits: “Money certainly has an impact. But the Republicans are so underwater that it’s hard to make up that gap with money alone.”

Musk’s post was not a reply to Domer. In a separate post about 40 minutes later, he wrote: “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” with a shrugging emoji after.

The joke refers to comments that Ashley St. Clair—the mother of one of Musk’s children—made to filmmaker Alex Gibney for a recent documentary, citing what she claimed Musk said following President Donald Trump’s 2024 election win. Musk has threatened to sue Gibney for defamation over the film, which is highly critical of the tech titan.

Polymarket Had Talarico as the Favorite

Polymarket traders had leaned toward Talarico for days. The market priced a Republican win at 28.5% on Oct. 30 and 25.5% as polls opened on Election Day, Nov. 3, implying odds of roughly 71.5% and 74.5% for the Democrat. The Texas Senate winner event drew about $21.8 million in trading volume.

The result was part of a broader Democratic surge that gave the party control of both the Senate and the House. For Domer, buying “No” at nearly 75 cents a share meant a large stake for a roughly 34% return, on an outcome the market already favored.

Talarico’s win also drew comment from Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor, who wrote on X that Texas “elected a Democratic senator who voted to create” a bitcoin reserve for his state. As a state representative, Talarico voted for the bill creating Texas’ Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, which the state House passed 101-42 in May 2025.

“The case for holding bitcoin crosses party lines,” Saylor wrote.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Bitcoin fell below $76,000 as US stocks reversed their post-election gains, France’s National Assembly rejected a budget revenue bill containing proposed crypto tax measures and Democrats threatened investigations into President Donald Trump’s crypto ventures.

Bitcoin crashes 6% to 7-week low as US stocks erase election gains

Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $76,000 on Thursday as risk assets abruptly reversed their US midterm elections rally. After making swift gains on the back of a Democrat sweep of the US House of Representatives and Senate, equities saw sharp selling on Thursday as traders rotated out of tech.

Crypto markets liquidated nearly $500 million in positioning in the first hour of the US trading session, per data from CoinGlass, with 24-hour total liquidations nearing $850 million.

Now targeting $76,000, BTC/USD approached the bottom of its one-month trading range. The pair risked losing support at the 50-week simple moving average (SMA), currently at $75,733.

In his latest analysis, crypto trader Rekt Capital noted that Bitcoin was repeating behavior from May, when a period of rangebound moves around $80,000 subsequently gave way to a breakdown and new macro lows of $57,000 in late June.

France budget rejection sidelines stablecoin tax, wallet reporting

The French National Assembly rejected the 2027 state budget’s revenue section late Wednesday, removing crypto-related amendments from the version of the bill sent to the Senate.

The Assembly rejected the revenue section by a vote of 458–0 at first reading, with two abstentions, according to the official voting record. The revenue section covers government income, such as taxes.

After the rejection, the government will send the Senate the original budget text, without the crypto-related amendments adopted by lawmakers.

The proposals could still be reintroduced in the Senate and would need to survive the remaining budget process to become law.

Faustine Fleuret, global head of public affairs at lending protocol Morpho, told Cointelegraph before the vote that rejection of the revenue section could “result in the rejection of the entire bill in the National Assembly, including provisions adopted by way of amendments.”

‘Lawyer up’: Democrats target Trump, Big Tech after midterm sweep

Democratic lawmakers said Big Tech executives should expect a wave of subpoenas, along with investigations into US President Donald Trump’s business circle when the new Congress takes office in January. 

As Democrats secured control of Congress in a sweeping victory on Tuesday, Democratic lawmakers were already firing warning shots at the Trump family and tech executives close to the US president. 

“They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we’ll be printing,” said US Senator Ed Markey, who sits on the Senate Commerce Committee, referring to Big Tech executives. 

US Representative Robert Garcia, the expected incoming House Oversight Committee chairman, said he plans to take on “the Trump Crime Family, corporate corruption, DHS and ICE abuses, and the cover-up of the Epstein files,” adding a two-word warning: “Lawyer up.” 

The warnings follow a mid-term election campaign in which Democrats challenged Big Tech’s growing political influence and the rapid expansion of AI, raising concerns about data centers’ demands on electricity, safeguards for AI products and tech executives’ ties to Trump.

title: American Bitcoin’s $126M profit masks mining pressure as rivals turn to AI
summary: The Eric Trump-backed miner reported $126 million in quarterly net income, largely driven by gains on its Bitcoin holdings, despite rising mining costs and shrinking margins.
content:
American Bitcoin reported a quarterly net income of $126 million on Wednesday, but rising mining costs and falling profits from mining raise questions about its long-term strategy as major rivals pivot towards artificial intelligence.

The Eric Trump-backed company’s profit was driven by a $197.3 million noncash gain on its Bitcoin (BTC) holdings. Meanwhile, mining revenue fell 5.5% to $63.4 million from the previous quarter, while the cost to mine one BTC rose about 15% to $42,100.

Excluding gains from its Bitcoin holdings, American Bitcoin would have reported an operating loss of approximately $5.5 million, according to its financial statements. The company also recorded a separate $64.3 million loss on derivatives.

“Despite seasonal power cost pressures, we continued mining Bitcoin at a structural discount to spot,” American Bitcoin CEO Mike Ho said in Wednesday’s earnings announcement.

Earnings per share stood at $1.73, beating analysts’ consensus estimate of $0.26, according to Yahoo Finance data.

Bitcoin was trading at $76,119, down 5% over the past 24 hours as of 8:50 p.m. UTC, according to CoinGecko data. Shares of American Bitcoin (ABTC), meanwhile, closed Thursday down about 15% at $5.31.

The results highlight an interesting divide among Bitcoin miners: while American Bitcoin continues mining and holding BTC, competitors like Riot Platforms, MARA Holdings and Core Scientific are investing in AI to find new sources of revenue.

Mining margins narrow

David Gamble, founder of asset management company Enigma Holdings, which focuses on Bitcoin mining and AI infrastructure, said American Bitcoin’s reported profit does not tell the full story of its mining business.

“Ultimately, mining Bitcoin below its market price doesn’t automatically mean you’re creating shareholder value,” Gamble told Cointelegraph.

American Bitcoin’s gross mining profit fell to $25.8 million from $33 million in the previous quarter. Its reported mining margin dropped to 41% from 49%, leaving the company with a smaller share of mining revenue after direct costs.

The company’s $63.4 million in quarterly revenue also fell short of analysts’ estimates of $74.35 million, according to Yahoo Finance data, a gap of nearly 15%.

The company mined 891 BTC during the quarter, down from 932 BTC in the previous three months. It also said higher electricity prices were the main reason mining costs increased.

“I don’t necessarily think their accumulation strategy is flawed, but I do think it raises questions about long-term sustainability,” Gamble said, pointing to increasing mining difficulty and the need to keep investing in newer and more efficient technology to compete.

Compared with the same period last year, revenue was nearly unchanged, falling from $64.2 million to $63.4 million. Reported profit, however, jumped from $3.5 million to $126 million, largely reflecting gains on the company’s Bitcoin holdings.

Related: Bitcoin miners face widening AI financing costs as lenders scrutinize deals

Rivals turn to AI as American Bitcoin builds reserves

American Bitcoin’s strategy comes as competitors like Riot Platforms, MARA Holdings and Core Scientific rapidly expand into AI.

Riot is building large AI data centers, according to its latest earnings. Meanwhile MARA is expanding into AI while continuing to mine Bitcoin. Core Scientific, on the other hand, has already shifted much of its business toward AI data centers.

American Bitcoin, by contrast, continues building its BTC reserves, holding 8,427 BTC at the end of September, up from 3,418 BTC a year earlier.

“The real competitive advantage in this industry is shifting toward energy infrastructure,” Gamble said. “It’s no longer just about how much Bitcoin you can mine or how much hashrate you can deploy.”

Gamble also explained that Bitcoin miners and AI companies are competing for the same power supply, and AI data centers could make more money than Bitcoin mining in some areas.

“That doesn’t mean every mining facility can simply transition into AI,” he said. “You still have to account for depreciation, equipment replacement, financing costs, and the opportunity cost of deploying that capital elsewhere.”

title: Asian crypto exchanges batten down the hatches as hacks surge: Asia Express
summary: Asian crypto exchanges are scrambling to tighten security on fears of a wave of potentially AI-assisted hacks, even as regional governments embrace tokenization and stablecoins.
content:
India warns AI-powered hackers targeting crypto exchanges at ‘machine speed’

India’s national cybersecurity agency warned that an AI-assisted threat actor has escalated its attacks on cryptocurrency exchanges and other financial businesses, stealing wallet keys and siphoning funds.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on Wednesday designated the threat actor as “CRAFTY FALCON” and explicitly identified crypto exchanges among affected businesses.

“The threat is active and ongoing. CSIRT-Fin continues to receive reports of successful attacks, including from NBFCs and fintech entities that had already received the earlier restricted advisories and had undertaken remediation,” said CERT-In. 

The warning adds to evidence of hackers using AI tools against financial institutions. In October, cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike reported that an unidentified attacker used ARTEX, an AI penetration-testing tool also named in CERT-In’s advisory, alongside Claude Code and other AI models to breach South Korean financial firms and steal data.

SOUTH KOREA

South Korea urges exchanges to boost cold storage after Binance hack

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has urged domestic crypto exchanges to increase the proportion of assets held in cold wallets after the $6.3 billion attack on Binance. 

The FSC said it held an emergency meeting with other regulators, cybersecurity agencies and crypto service providers to review security measures. 

It reviewed exchanges’ IT access controls, wallet withdrawal approval and signing procedures, and administrator privileges. It also urged providers to increase the proportion of assets held in offline cold wallets.

But South Korean law already requires exchanges to hold at least 80% of users’ crypto assets in cold storage, with Upbit keeping 99.17% assets in cold wallets, followed by Bithumb at 94.76% and Coinone at 85%.

Bank of Korea probes financial firms’ exposure to crypto risks

The Bank of Korea is surveying 31 financial institutions on how a major exchange shutdown, prolonged crypto downturn or losses at another firm could affect their operations.

One scenario asks how financial firms would be affected if South Korea’s largest crypto exchange by market share temporarily suspended operations following a major hack or similar incident.

Other questions address a steep fall in cryptocurrency prices followed by a sustained trading slump, and the potential fallout if another financial institution suffered heavy losses from a crypto-related incident.

‘Absurd rhetoric’: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack

Despite clear evidence of years of North Korea-linked hacking groups stealing billions from crypto exchanges, Pyongyang claims to have had no involvement in the $6.3 billion Binance hack and floated the idea it was actually the Americans.

“The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a ‘cyber criminal state’, claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in the incident,” said Kim Yo Jong said. “But the US assertion is an absurd rhetoric and nothing new.”

South Korea targets 2029 for the next time it will delay its crypto tax

South Korea’s government has backed postponing tax on cryptocurrency gains by another two years to 2029. Judging on the troubled history of the tax, it would not be surprising if it is delayed again at that point.

HONG KONG

Crypto.com to withdraw Hong Kong consumer app citing regulatory changes

Crypto.com will discontinue its consumer app services in Hong Kong on Feb. 1, 2027, while continuing to pursue regulatory approval for its institutional exchange.

A Crypto.com spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company would discontinue its consumer app services in Hong Kong. The spokesperson said all affected customers had received advance notice and would receive instructions on closing their accounts and support to withdraw their funds.

Nearly three years after the local entity submitted an application for a license and the status remains “deemed-to-be-licensed” — which a transitional status rather than full regulatory approval.

Animoca Brands clears final hurdle for Abu Dhabi fund management

The Hong Kong headquartered Animoca Brands has secured approval to manage investment funds for non-retail clients in Abu Dhabi.

The authorization, granted to subsidiary Animoca Asset Management (AD) Limited by Abu Dhabi Global Market’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA), allows it to oversee funds that pool money from professional investors rather than the general public.

It expanding the asset management business of a company that began in mobile games before moving into blockchain gaming, rode the Metaverse wave and was a big player in venture investing.

Hong Kong takes tokenized settlement to 24/7, plans stablecoin trials

Hong Kong has expanded its Project Ensemble pilot to allow round-the-clock settlement of tokenized transactions, as the city’s monetary regulator prepares to bring regulated stablecoins into trials involving tokenized government debt.

Hong Kong opens secondary trading for tokenized funds

Hong Kong has recently officially introduced secondary market trading for SFC-authorised Tokenized Funds through licensed exchanges. Two China Asset Management money-market funds can now trade continuously via PantherTrade and the Futubull app.

THAILAND

Thailand to block Bitget in December over unlicensed crypto trading

Thailand’s securities regulator has filed a criminal complaint against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, for allegedly operating without a license. Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission will block access to the website and app from December 5.

According to the SEC, Bitget offered crypto trading services between 2022 and 2025, charged trading fees and promoted its services in Thai through its websites and social media channels. The regulator said these activities violated Thailand’s digital asset business licensing requirements.

The regulator advised users to take action regarding assets held on the platform before the deadline.

AUSTRALIA

Australia lifts rates to 18-year high as AI boom, energy costs fuel inflation

Australia’s central bank raised its interest rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% on Tuesday, warning that inflation would stay elevated through much of 2027 as energy costs and AI-related investment added to price pressures.

The Reserve Bank of Australia’s monetary policy board voted 6–3 for the increase, with three members preferring to hold rates at 4.60%.

The bank pushed back its forecast for inflation to return to the top of its 2% to 3% target range until late 2027, around three quarters later than previously expected.

How Aussie Bitcoiners can avoid 2027’s shock CGT hike

The Australian government’s decision to scrap the 50% capital gains discount for all investments in the May budget came as a big shock for crypto owners. The new scheme effectively doubles the taxable component of a gain, minus a small discount for inflation.

Some Aussie crypto holders are taking drastic measures — like Finder founder and crypto king Fred Schebesta who is relocating to Singapore which offers 0% CGT, stating the tax changes were a “killer blow.”


But there are less dramatic methods to reduce CGT bills including setting up a self managed super fund (SMSF), a company to trade crypto at the company tax rate, or to hope the opposition will reverse the changes after the next election.

JAPAN

JPYC marks first year but undershoots target by three quarters

Japanese yen stablecoin JPYC marked its first anniversary with a circulating supply around 3 billion yen—one quarter of its internal target.

BlackRock and SBI sign yen-stablecoin tokenised fund MOU

title: Arkansas Sues Kalshi, Alleging Deceptive Trading Practices and Unjust Enrichment
summary: Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin introduced a lawsuit that alleges Kalshi knowingly lied to customers in Arkansas, presenting its platform as legal and safe while violating the state’s Deceptive Trade Practices Act by offering unlicensed gambling products and making its services available to un...
content:
Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin introduced a lawsuit that alleges Kalshi knowingly lied to customers in Arkansas, presenting its platform as legal and safe while violating the state’s Deceptive Trade Practices Act by offering unlicensed gambling products and making its services available to underage users.

Key Takeaways

  • Arkansas sued prediction platform Kalshi for allegedly operating an unlicensed and deceptive state gambling business.
  • The state seeks to immediately halt Kalshi’s operations, mandate consumer restitution, and collect fines.
  • Arkansas joins multiple states fighting federal CFTC authority over the legality of event betting markets.

Arkansas Sues Kalshi, Joins Other States In Semantics Battle

Kalshi, one of the largest prediction market platforms in the U.S. with billions in volumes traded, is being sued by Arkansas for its involvement in illegal gambling practices.

On Wednesday, Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin filed a lawsuit against KalshiEX LLC and Kalshi Inc., the owners and operators of the prediction market platform Kalshi, alleging they violated the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act by offering event products without a license to operate in the state.

Griffin claims that while Kalshi offered its services as event contracts, they constitute unlicensed forms of sports betting and casino gaming, bypassing the state framework to comply with Arkansas regulation. Furthermore, the state alleges that Kalshi allowed underage users to access these products, violating the state’s 21-year-old limit for involvement in these activities.

Finally, Arkansas says Kalshi deceived users by claiming its platform was regulated and legal while knowingly omitting the risks of professional and insider trading in its operations.

Griffin stressed that Arkansas law was concerned “with substance and not with semantics,” and that the gambling activity was regulated to protect customers.

“It doesn’t take a genius to understand that wagering money on whether the Razorbacks win or lose is gambling. And gambling on an unregulated platform is squarely prohibited by Arkansas law,” he explained.

“Kalshi is not blind that its platform presents real, tangible risks to its users, including excessive wagering, financial losses, depression, and other mental health harms. That’s why I have brought this lawsuit today to hold Kalshi accountable for multiple violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act,” Griffin concluded.

Initially, Arkansas seeks confirmation that Kalshi violated state gambling laws and an injunction to halt the company’s operations in the state. It also asks for restitution to consumers suffering financial losses and disgorgement of the funds the company acquired through unjust enrichment.

Financially, Arkansas calls for maximum civil penalties in accordance with state law, reaching up to $10,000 per violation, to recover unpaid taxes since the company started operating in Arkansas, and to pay for the lawsuit fees and costs.

Arkansas is the latest state to dispute the notion that event markets do not constitute gambling, with the company already facing similar allegations in Utah, Missouri, Tennessee, and New York, setting up a federal vs. state law fight where the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has also filed lawsuits against some states.

The CFTC has claimed it holds exclusive jurisdiction to regulation prediction markets, but states continue to challenge that claim. A coalition of 44 state AGs has alleged that the CFTC lacks authority over these markets, as it “drastically expands federal regulatory authority in an area of major economic and political consequence that states have traditionally regulated.”

title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $76,000 as Nasdaq Tumbles into Correction
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Trades Near $76,000 as Nasdaq Tumbles into Correction
Bitcoin price held near $76,000 Thursday afternoon as the Nasdaq sank deeper into a correction, crypto liquidations topped $1 billion and Strategy, Coinbase and bitcoin miners sold off in double digits.
This post B...
content:
Bitcoin price traded near $76,000 on Thursday afternoon, down more than 5% on the day after sliding through the mid-$75,000s as a Nasdaq-led selloff in chip and AI stocks deepened into a formal correction and forced out more than $1 billion in leveraged bets, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows.

The afternoon session extended the morning crash that had already erased overnight gains above $80,000. Bitcoin briefly tested support near $75,400 before stabilizing just under $76,000 into the final hour of U.S. cash trading.

Bitcoin near $75,900 in afternoon trade, on track for its biggest single-day slide since June. The move undid Wednesday’s short-squeeze bounce in a single session. Traders who bought the midterm rebound with borrowed money were the first forced out when stocks cracked at the open, and the bitcoin price never regained the $77,000 area that held as morning support.

Nasdaq’s correction pulls crypto lower

Wall Street set the tone. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% on Thursday and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below the record close it set last month, CNBC reported. The S&P 500 lost roughly 4%, and the Dow shed more than 1,600 points.

Semiconductors led the rout. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index sank about 11%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF posted its biggest one-day drop since March 2020. Nvidia and Broadcom each fell around 9%, Qualcomm lost about 9% and Tesla dropped about 11%.

Investors are pricing in a slower AI data-center buildout under a Democratic Congress. Traders fear construction pauses and tighter financing for neoclouds, a risk that has weighed on chip and infrastructure names since the midterm results. Analysts told CNBC that the $1.2 trillion of AI capital spending forecast for next year is now being reworked.

Bitcoin has moved with that AI-heavy complex for most of the year. Miners that sold bitcoin to fund data centers are now caught in both trades, so political risk on power and construction hits the same names that used to trade mainly on the bitcoin price.

Leverage flush grows past $1 billion

Forced selling kept the bitcoin price under pressure into the afternoon. Roughly $1.08 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including about $954 million in long bets, as futures markets unwound positions built during Wednesday’s short squeeze.

Nearly $900 million of that wipeout came in a roughly four-hour stretch after the U.S. open, turning a stock-led break into a cascade of margin calls. Ether fell below $2,300 as the same leverage flushed out.

Crypto equities followed. Strategy (MSTR), Coinbase (COIN) and Circle (CRCL) each fell more than 10%, and bitcoin miners dropped as much as 20%. Keel Infrastructure (KEEL), which sold its entire bitcoin treasury for $192 million, slid about 20%. CleanSpark (CLSK), Cipher (CIFR) and TeraWulf (WULF) each lost more than 12%.

What comes next for bitcoin price

The next test is Friday’s October jobs report, then October CPI on Nov. 10 and the Fed’s Dec. 9 decision. Policy risk is building too, with House Democrats drafting their own market structure bill ahead of taking the committees in January.

Traders are watching whether the bitcoin price can hold the mid-$75,000 area that served as support on election night and several times since August. A clean break would leave bitcoin with room to run lower, near its weakest levels in months and put the September low back in view.

Options markets have been quiet into the jobs print, but the cash market is not. Volume stayed elevated through the afternoon as stocks and crypto sold together rather than against each other.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $75,900.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Crypto ally French Hill wins reelection but set to lose House chair
summary: Republican French Hill secured another term in Congress but will lose his leadership of the House Financial Services Committee when Democrats take control in January.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 5, 2026

Republican French Hill secured another term in Congress but will lose his leadership of the House Financial Services Committee when Democrats take control in January.

House Financial Services Committee Chair French Hill, a key Republican ally of the cryptocurrency industry, has won reelection in Arkansas but is expected to lose his committee chairmanship after Democrats won control of the House of Representatives in Tuesday’s midterm elections.

The Associated Press called the race Thursday, confirming Hill’s victory over Democratic challenger Chris Jones in Arkansas’ 2nd Congressional District. Hill, who sponsored the CLARITY Act and voted for the GENIUS Act, holds an A rating from the crypto advocacy group Stand With Crypto, which classifies him as strongly supportive of cryptocurrency.

Fairshake, a cryptocurrency industry-backed super political action committee (PAC), pledged $1 million to support Hill’s reelection campaign in October as part of its efforts to retain crypto-friendly lawmakers in Congress.

California Democrat Maxine Waters, the current ranking member of the House Financial Services Committee, is the leading contender to replace Hill as chair, according to Reuters reporting.

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections, raising uncertainty over the future of US crypto legislation and the prospect of increased industry scrutiny. Crypto-backed super PACs spent more than $176 million during the election cycle.

title: Canary Capital Brings Injective to Nasdaq With New INJ Staked ETF
summary: Canary Capital has launched an exchange-traded fund for Injective’s INJ token, allowing investors to gain exposure to the cryptocurrency and earn potential staking rewards. Meeting Demand for Specialized Blockchain Networks Digital asset investment management firm Canary Capital has launched an exch...
content:
Canary Capital has launched an exchange-traded fund for Injective’s INJ token, allowing investors to gain exposure to the cryptocurrency and earn potential staking rewards.

Key Takeaways

  • Canary Capital launched a Staked INJ ETF to give traditional investors exposure and staking rewards.
  • Injective processed 3.13 billion transactions and burned over 7.27 million INJ, boosting institutional adoption.
  • The ETF expects to broaden access to onchain markets for traditional accounts by November 2026.

Meeting Demand for Specialized Blockchain Networks

Digital asset investment management firm Canary Capital has launched an exchange-traded fund (ETF) based on Injective (INJ), providing investors exposure to the cryptocurrency through traditional brokerage accounts. In addition, the product offers potential returns from blockchain staking rewards.

The firm’s CEO, Steven McClurg, said the launch expands Canary Capital’s digital asset investment offerings, which include the Canary XRP ETF and Canary HBAR ETF. It also reflects growing institutional interest in cryptocurrency products that combine price exposure with staking rewards.

“The Canary Staked INJ ETF gives investors access to a blockchain purpose-built for finance through a familiar exchange-traded structure, while also enabling investors to benefit from potential staking rewards,” McClurg said.

McClurg added that investors are increasingly looking beyond established cryptocurrencies toward specialized blockchain networks supporting emerging financial applications, including tokenization, trading, and decentralized markets.

According to a press release, Injective has tokenized more than $1 billion in assets, positioning the network among blockchain platforms pursuing the market for tokenized financial instruments. As of Oct. 22, the network had processed more than 3.13 billion transactions and permanently burned over 7.27 million INJ, valued at approximately $58 million, through its token buyback mechanisms.

Data from analytics platform Token Terminal showed approximately 257,300 monthly active addresses on Injective as of October.

INJ is one of the biggest gainers in the top 100 cryptocurrencies over the last 24 hours, recently up about 5% at a price of $8.23, pushing its weekly gain to 10%. The daily uptick comes amid the ETF launch—and a broader crypto market decline mirroring a tech stock sell-off. Bitcoin is down about 5% on the day at a price above $76,000.

Bridging Traditional Finance and Onchain Markets

The network has introduced several upgrades aimed at expanding institutional adoption. These include Injective Mint, which enables institutions to issue and manage tokenized assets with customizable ownership and transfer restrictions. Another initiative, CypherOS, provides privacy-focused infrastructure designed to support confidential trading, transactions and asset tokenization.

Meanwhile, more than $25 million in native USDC stablecoins had been issued on Injective as of October, supporting payment and settlement activities across the network.

Eric Chen, co-founder of the Injective Foundation, said the ETF would make INJ accessible to a broader investor base without requiring direct interaction with cryptocurrency exchanges or blockchain wallets.

“Investors can now gain exposure to INJ through the brokerage accounts they already use,” Chen said. “We built Injective to bring financial markets onchain. Canary’s launch connects that mission to a broader base of investors, giving them a familiar way to access the asset that powers Injective.”

title: Gate Pioneers Proof of Security (PoSEC), Achieving 104.58% Cold Storage Coverage to Solidify Asset Security
summary: Gate has officially introduced Proof of Security (PoSEC), a new asset security verification framework, becoming the first digital asset trading platform in the industry to launch a PoSEC security verification system. Since its founding in 2013, Gate has consistently placed user asset security at the...
content:
Gate has officially introduced Proof of Security (PoSEC), a new asset security verification framework, becoming the first digital asset trading platform in the industry to launch a PoSEC security verification system. Since its founding in 2013, Gate has consistently placed user asset security at the forefront of its priorities. With the introduction of PoSEC, Gate extends security verification beyond reserve adequacy to include asset storage structures and risk coverage capabilities, further solidifying safeguards for user assets and providing a new practical approach to advancing industry security standards.

PoSEC Focuses on Asset Storage Security and Quantifies Extreme-Risk Coverage Capabilities

Unlike Proof of Reserves (PoR), which primarily verifies the adequacy of asset reserves, PoSEC places additional emphasis on asset storage security. By publicly disclosing the distribution of assets between platform cold storage and hot wallets, PoSEC provides visibility into asset storage structures and their ability to cover potential losses under extreme scenarios.

PoSEC introduces the cold storage coverage ratio as a key metric to measure the extent to which cold storage covers total user assets. A coverage ratio ≥ 100% means that, under the applicable calculation methodology, cold storage alone would be sufficient to cover all user assets even if all assets held in hot wallets were lost. PoR and PoSEC serve complementary purposes, extending asset security verification from reserve adequacy to storage security and risk coverage, while providing users with more comprehensive and transparent information about asset security.

Cold Storage Coverage Reaches 104.58%, with Open and Transparent Storage Structure

According to the snapshot taken at 00:00 (UTC) on November 4, 2026, Gate’s cold storage coverage ratio reached 104.58%, with cold storage and hot wallet assets accounting for 88.26% and 11.74% of total assets, respectively. Cold storage assets include digital assets held offline and traditional assets under independent custody. To qualify, these assets must meet requirements such as not being directly used for routine deposits and withdrawals, being held offline or under independent custody, requiring multi-party authorization for transfers, and being independently verifiable.

The current data is undergoing verification by an independent third-party audit firm. The review covers asset authenticity and control, valuation and calculation methodologies, and coverage ratio calculations. The audit report will be published on Gate’s official website upon completion, enhancing the transparency and credibility of asset security disclosures.

From PoR to PoSEC: Continuously Strengthening Digital Asset Security

Gate has long been committed to digital asset security and transparency. In 2020, Gate was among the first in the industry to introduce an open-source Proof of Reserves (PoR) mechanism and a Merkle Tree-based asset verification solution, establishing itself as an early contributor to reserve transparency in the industry. Gate subsequently incorporated technologies such as zk-SNARKs to enhance its asset reserve verification framework.

As of October 18, 2026, Gate’s total reserves amounted to approximately $8.688 billion, with an overall reserve ratio of 118.49%. The platform also employs a range of security mechanisms, including hot and cold wallet segregation, multi-signature technology, Multi-Party Computation (MPC), dynamic risk monitoring, and zero-trust access control, to establish a multi-layered security framework covering asset reserves, storage management, and risk protection.

From PoR, which verifies reserve adequacy, to PoSEC, which verifies asset storage security and risk coverage capabilities, Gate is progressively building a multi-layered security framework encompassing asset reserves, storage management, risk protection, and public verification. Looking ahead, Gate will continue to uphold its security-first principle, further develop PoSEC standards and verification mechanisms, and collaborate with more industry participants to enhance asset security and transparency, laying a stronger security foundation for the long-term, sustainable development of the digital asset industry.

Learn more: https://www.gate.com/proof-of-security

About Gate

Gate, founded in 2013 by Dr. Han, is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency and integrated financial services platforms, spanning financial and everyday use cases including asset management, trading and payments. Serving over 62 million users globally, it supports trading across 5,400+ digital assets and 12,800+ stock assets and ETFs, while providing access to a comprehensive range of TradFi assets, including metals, stocks, indices, forex, and commodities to meet users’ end-to-end needs across asset holding, trading, and spending. As an industry benchmark, Gate was among the first platforms to implement 100% Proof of Reserves. Its ecosystem includes Gate Money, Gate Wallet, Gate Ventures, Gate for AI Agent, and a wide range of products and services.

title: Core Scientific (CORZ) to Exit Bitcoin Mining by Year-End as Colocation Hits $215 Million
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Core Scientific (CORZ) to Exit Bitcoin Mining by Year-End as Colocation Hits $215 Million
Core Scientific will finish winding down bitcoin mining in the fourth quarter and enter 2027 as a pure-play AI colocation landlord, with self-mining revenue already down to $12.3 million.
This...
content:
Core Scientific will complete its exit from bitcoin mining by year-end and enter 2027 as a pure-play high-density colocation provider, management said on Thursday’s third-quarter earnings call, capping a pivot that has already cut the company’s mining fleet nearly in half.

Chief Financial Officer Jim Nygaard told investors the company expects to “complete the wind-down during the fourth quarter.” Chief Executive Officer Adam Sullivan put the same end date more bluntly: “We expect to complete our exit from Bitcoin mining by year end.” The comments landed alongside a results release filed with the SEC that shows how far the shift has already gone.

Colocation revenue climbed nearly 60% sequentially to $215.4 million in the quarter ended Sept. 30, the earnings exhibit shows. Digital asset self-mining revenue fell to $12.3 million, down about 79% from $57.4 million a year earlier. Hosted mining for third parties added just $5.2 million. Of $232.9 million in total revenue, colocation now accounts for roughly 92%.

Self-mining posted a $7.5 million gross loss in the quarter. Colocation gross profit was $128.4 million, a 60% margin. Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled sequentially to $133.6 million, with the margin expanding to 57% from 25%.

Mining shrinks as AI leases fill the floor

Nygaard said Core Scientific had nearly 50% fewer miners online at the end of September than at year-end 2025. The company has been repurposing power and floor space under long-term customer agreements for AI and high-performance computing workloads, a process its investor materials describe as continuing “as circumstances allow.”

That path is not unique among public miners. Peers have been selling bitcoin and leasing campuses to AI tenants, and research notes have flagged a widening funding gap between those that can finance data center builds and those that cannot.

Core Scientific is billing for 485 megawatts of colocation capacity as of Sept. 30 — up 90 MW in the quarter — representing more than $700 million in average annualized colocation GAAP revenue. The remaining roughly 100 MW under its CoreWeave buildout is in commissioning and expected to start recognizing revenue over the next few months, Sullivan said.

Beyond CoreWeave’s contracted 590 MW, Core Scientific has 530 MW under an AMD-backed agreement across five campuses, with initial delivery targeted for the first half of 2027 and full delivery by the end of 2028. Together, the two relationships cover about 1.1 GW. Once fully delivered and billing, management expects that portfolio alone to generate $1.8 billion in average annual run-rate revenue and $1.6 billion in net operating income.

What Core Scientific’s sheet shows

Bitcoin is almost gone from the books. Digital assets stood at $2.7 million on Sept. 30, down from $49.7 million three months earlier and $222 million at year-end 2025. Earlier this year, Core Scientific was still adding coins even as it sold into the pivot; that chapter is effectively closed.

The mining exit has already carried a cash cost. A $41.9 million loss on contract termination booked in the second quarter reflects the decision to end a Block/Proto mining chip supply agreement. Liquidity ended the third quarter at about $1.7 billion, including roughly $800 million in cash, after heavy capital spending on AMD sites and the Polaris acquisition.

Sullivan framed the wind-down as simplifying the business toward “more attractive long-term growth opportunities.” Nygaard added that starting 2027 with a “very clean P&L” — one without mining in the numbers — should give investors a clearer look at a true colocation run-rate.

The test now is whether Core Scientific turns the last machines off on schedule in the fourth quarter, and whether the AMD financing package lands in time to keep that clean P&L growing.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Chainalysis Breach Exposes Passwords and Tokens for All Users, Forcing Service Shutdowns
summary: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis has disclosed that hackers accessed password hashes and active authentication tokens for all users of its platform, prompting the company to shut down several major services as it responds to an ongoing cyberattack. In its latest update, published Wednesday, Nov...
content:
Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis has disclosed that hackers accessed password hashes and active authentication tokens for all users of its platform, prompting the company to shut down several major services as it responds to an ongoing cyberattack.

Key Takeaways

  • Chainalysis disclosed a major data breach exposing password hashes and active authentication tokens for all users, expanding on its initial Oct. 30 report of compromised customer information.
  • The company shut down several critical services, including KYT transaction monitoring, address screening, Reactor, and Data Solutions, after detecting suspicious activity and unauthorized account access.
  • Chainalysis plans to restore services with enhanced security measures, including mandatory password resets, API key rotations and IP allowlisting.

In its latest update, published Wednesday, Nov. 4, at 11 p.m. ET, Chainalysis said it discovered on Monday that customer information—including names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens—had been exposed to a malicious actor. The company also confirmed suspicious activity involving its compliance monitoring products, raising concerns about the broader scope of the breach.

The disclosure represents a significant escalation from the company’s initial Oct. 30 announcement, when Chainalysis reported that hackers had accessed basic customer information but said there was no evidence of compromised authentication credentials or investigation data.

Chainalysis said it has now taken its Know Your Transaction (KYT) monitoring platform offline, including its user interface and API, along with address screening products and its login page. Its Reactor investigation platform, Data Solutions products and Chain (Beta) service have also been shut down.

The company said it detected abnormal activity in its transaction screening systems after introducing additional monitoring measures. It is directly notifying customers whose KYT accounts appear to have been accessed without authorization.

Despite the escalating security concerns, Chainalysis said it has not found evidence that confidential investigation data was accessed or that its blockchain attribution data was manipulated.

The company plans to begin restoring KYT and Address Screening access on Thursday, Nov. 5, using a system that requires customers to provide trusted IP addresses for an allowlist. Customers will then be able to reset passwords and rotate API keys. Chainalysis said all users will be required to reset their passwords and rotate API keys where appropriate as part of the broader restoration process.

AI-Assisted Attack Exposes Customer Information

Chainalysis first disclosed the incident on Oct. 30, explaining that it had detected an external attacker using what it described as “offensive agentic techniques” to gain unauthorized access to internal systems and tools.

The terminology suggests the attacker employed autonomous or AI-assisted techniques, although the company has not provided a technical explanation of how those methods were used or identified the vulnerabilities initially exploited.

At the time, Chainalysis acknowledged that user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organizational role information had been accessed. It characterized those records as non-sensitive and said it was determining how many customers were affected.

However, Wednesday’s updates revealed considerably more serious exposure.

Earlier in the day, Chainalysis confirmed that an “on-path attack” had compromised passwords belonging to a subset of customers. Such attacks involve intercepting communications between systems or users, potentially allowing attackers to capture sensitive information.

The company said that particular attack method had been contained and remediated, and it began notifying affected customers that their accounts would be locked until passwords were changed.

Hours later, Chainalysis disclosed the exposure of password hashes and live tokens for all users, substantially expanding the potential impact beyond the initially identified group.

The company has not disclosed how many individual users or organizations were affected, how long the attackers maintained access, or whether the exposed tokens were used to compromise additional accounts.

Security Incident Disrupts Critical Crypto Infrastructure

The breach is particularly significant because Chainalysis provides blockchain intelligence and compliance tools to cryptocurrency exchanges, financial institutions, regulators, and law enforcement agencies.

Its Reactor platform helps investigators trace cryptocurrency movements and examine connections between blockchain addresses, while KYT enables businesses to monitor transactions for potential money laundering, sanctions exposure, and other illicit activity.

The shutdown of these systems could disrupt investigations and compliance operations at organizations that rely on Chainalysis, although the company has not quantified the impact on customers.

The firm initially kept its transaction monitoring products operating while taking other services offline, citing their importance in detecting financial crime. That decision changed Wednesday after additional suspicious activity was identified.

Chainalysis has engaged outside cybersecurity specialists, and said it is also employing advanced large language models to examine its systems and strengthen defenses.

The company emphasized that the intrusion was unrelated to last week’s $6.3 billion crypto theft at leading exchange Binance, which has drawn significant attention across the industry. Earlier this week, Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin was separately targeted, with the company saying about $38 million in cryptocurrency was stolen.

Chainalysis has urged customers to remain alert for suspicious communications and unexpected authentication requests, enable two-factor authentication, and change passwords reused on other platforms. Its investigation remains ongoing, with additional disclosures possible as the company determines the full extent of the breach and works to restore its services.

title: FINRA Fines Webull $4.2M After 120K Accounts Bypassed Proper ID Checks
summary:
The Financial Industry
Regulatory Authority has fined Webull Financial LLC $4.2 million for failures
in its anti-money laundering, identity theft prevention and best execution
programmes.
London's trading industry is coming home!
FINRA found that
Webull approved more than 120,000 customer accounts b...
content:
2026-11-05T21:20:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 05/11/2026 | 19:20 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The regulator found the firm failed to investigate 473 unauthorised transfers worth more than $1.5 million.
  • One Webull account generated nearly 13,000 suspicious trading alerts without timely investigation.

The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority has fined Webull Financial LLC $4.2 million for failures in its anti-money laundering, identity theft prevention and best execution programmes.

London's trading industry is coming home!

FINRA found that Webull approved more than 120,000 customer accounts between January 2020 and September 2023 without adequately verifying applicants' identities.

Some accounts were approved using photographs of scenic landscapes instead of government-issued identification, while others belonged to applicants listed as deceased in Webull's own systems.

Webull Failed to Detect Suspicious Transactions

"Webull’s business grew rapidly, but its compliance program did not keep pace," said Bill St. Louis, FINRA's Executive Vice President and Head of Enforcement.

FINRA found that Webull failed to investigate 473 unauthorised Automated Clearing House transfers worth more than $1.5 million. The transfers moved funds from customers at other financial institutions into Webull accounts.

The broker also failed to investigate an account that generated nearly 13,000 alerts for potentially manipulative trading across more than 100 stock symbols over approximately 18 months.

Other surveillance gaps included inadequate monitoring of suspicious out-of-the-money options trading, customers using the same address or device, and fraudulent account takeovers.

Webull also opened dozens of accounts for foreign nationals using the same IP address or device. It did not introduce checks for unrelated accounts sharing the same Social Security number until August 2021.

title: Binance, Deribit revoke SignalPlus API keys after fake Teams invite attack
summary: SignalPlus said attackers compromised an engineer’s computer in a breach that resulted in losses of less than $82,000, which the crypto trading platform pledged to reimburse in full.
content:
Exchanges Binance and Deribit said Thursday they had revoked API keys connected to crypto derivatives trading platform SignalPlus as a precaution following a security breach. Both exchanges said their own systems were unaffected, while Deribit warned that trading, monitoring and automation through SignalPlus had stopped working for its customers.

Binance co-founder Yi He also urged third-party platforms integrated with the exchange to review their security controls and monitor for suspicious activity, warning that the threat extended beyond any single company.

SignalPlus provides trading infrastructure for crypto derivatives, particularly options, allowing professional and institutional traders to manage positions across multiple exchanges through a single platform.

According to the company on X, the attack originated from a compromised Telegram account belonging to a contact at a third-party technology vendor. The attacker impersonated the contact and sent a fake Microsoft Teams meeting invitation to a SignalPlus engineer, compromising the employee’s computer.

Source: SignalPlus

The attacker remained dormant on the compromised computer before using the engineer’s access privileges to target SignalPlus’s internal network early Wednesday, the company said.

SignalPlus said it detected and contained the intrusion, with total losses of less than $82,000, and had begun fully reimbursing affected users. The company temporarily suspended its services and expects to restore operations over the next few days after completing security reviews and applying patches.

SignalPlus also acknowledged that it had not required IP whitelisting for exchange API access. “We take responsibility for this oversight,” the company said, adding that it would tighten API access requirements and strengthen internal security controls. IP whitelisting is a security measure that restricts API access to a predefined list of approved internet addresses.

Related: BitMart founder says security team ‘severely understaffed’ after new hack

SignalPlus attack follows $6.3B Binance hack

The SignalPlus incident comes days after Binance disclosed details of a $6.3 billion hack on Oct. 29, which also involved compromised employee computers.

According to Binance’s postmortem, attackers posing as recruiters tricked an engineer into downloading a malicious file disguised as a coding assignment. The attackers subsequently used the compromised computer to gain access to additional systems and eventually breach the exchange’s wallet infrastructure.

Binance co-founder Yi He said Tuesday that the exchange had detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threats in 2026, including fraudulent job interviews, malicious software packages and attempts to steal employee credentials.

title: Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate
Greece's parliament approved a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the country's first dedicated crypto tax framework, with annual gains up to €500 exempt.
This post Greece Approves 10% Cr...
content:
Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country.

Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions.

“Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters.

An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal.

What the levy covers for bitcoin holders

The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation.

A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first.

Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins.

Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Greek analyses of the text say that once net gains clear that ceiling, the 10% rate applies to the full net gain for the year, not only the slice above €500. Losses above €500 in a tax year may be carried forward for up to five years and offset only against future crypto capital gains.

Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded.

An EU patchwork, not a single rate

European Union countries do not share a unified tax system for the sector. Rates on cryptocurrency gains typically run from about 8% to 30% across member states and are usually levied on capital gains, the finance ministry official said. Greece’s 10% sits toward the softer end of that band, below France’s often-cited 30% treatment and above Cyprus’s 8%.

The same patchwork is shifting elsewhere in the bloc. The Netherlands has moved toward a realized capital gains tax from 2028, while Germany and Portugal still exempt crypto held longer than a year. Since January, the EU’s DAC8 reporting rules have required crypto platforms to send user and transaction data to national tax authorities — a tool Greece already wrote into domestic law.

State revenue from the new levy could not be projected, the official said, because the vast majority of investors use platforms abroad, leaving the size of Greece’s cryptocurrency market hard to measure.

For bitcoin holders who trade on foreign exchanges, that gap is the practical test. The rate is now set in law; whether Athens can match 10% on paper with enforceable cost-basis data from offshore platforms is the question the coming directives will have to answer.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Conflux – Web3’s Next Billion Users
summary: David Wei Liang is a vice president at Conflux Network, the Layer-1 blockchain built around its Tree-Graph consensus and positioned as a bridge between China’s engineering ecosystem and global Web3 markets. His career has centred on distributed systems. He earned a PhD in computer science at the Chi...
content:
Skip to content

David Wei Liang is a vice president at Conflux Network, the Layer-1 blockchain built around its Tree-Graph consensus and positioned as a bridge between China’s engineering ecosystem and global Web3 markets. His career has centred on distributed systems. He earned a PhD in computer science at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, studying peer-to-peer networks, followed by postdoctoral research in distributed systems. He then worked at Huawei’s Noah’s Ark Lab in Hong Kong and became chief blockchain expert at China Telecom, where he led work on the blockchain-enabled SIM card, BSIM.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Most of crypto, Liang argues, competes for the same users and capital, moving them between chains with bridges, compatible tooling and higher yields. The larger opportunity sits outside that circle: close to six billion mobile subscribers, five billion internet users and billions of banking customers, plus a projected wave of AI agents that Huawei estimates could reach 900 billion by 2035. His view is that moving existing users only changes market share, while creating new demand changes the size of the market. Telecom operators, with decades of relationships with billions of subscribers and the physical networks every digital economy runs on, are in his view the most natural route in.

The practical case rests on BSIM, which turns the SIM card already in everyone’s phone into a secure wallet that generates and stores private keys and signs transactions without the keys ever leaving the card. Liang describes a pilot in Shanghai, a commercial deployment in Hong Kong through a licensed telecom operator combining roaming data and stablecoin payments, and an enterprise rollout with an insurance partner in Hunan. His main lesson is that people should not have to become crypto experts to use Web3, and that asking newcomers to write down a 12-word recovery phrase works against mass adoption. He sees digital identity as the most valuable starting point, linking a subscriber’s network identity to a wallet with consent, so that a phone number can work as a payment address and operators could reward users for everyday calls.

The conversation then moves to AI. Liang argues that agents need money software can spend in very small amounts and settle instantly, with spending limits enforced in code, and points to standards such as x402 that already make this possible. His rule for what belongs on-chain is simple: anything that needs speed stays off-chain, while anything that needs agreement, such as payments, commitments and settlement, goes on the ledger. On privacy, he argues that personal AI agents will learn far more about their users than Web2 platforms ever did, and that combining telecom identity, wallets and blockchain could let people authorize agents without handing their data to a few large companies. He closes with stablecoins including USDT0 and AxCNH now on Conflux, a network upgrade completed in October, and his test for success: Web3 wins when it disappears into everyday life, the way nobody says they are using TCP/IP.
