title: Fed, OCC check US banks after Binance hack as experts flag security risks
summary: US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance security hack, while experts raised concerns about transaction security and crypto risks.
content:
US regulators reportedly contacted banks following last week’s $6.3 billion Binance hack, as cybersecurity experts raised concerns about how financial institutions handle crypto-related security risks.

Officials from the Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) began contacting banks on Monday to ask about “unusual activity” or service disruptions, Reuters reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. 

The reported inquiries could be followed by closer attention to how banks manage crypto-related risks, including custody, counterparty exposure and incident response, according to Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK.

“After an incident of this scale, it would be surprising if the Fed and OCC didn’t check in with the banks they supervise,” Muehlbauer told Cointelegraph. “Their mandate is to protect the financial system, and that means understanding where exposures sit and how quickly they can respond.”

Banks review security systems after Binance hack

According to Reuters, banks have been assessing the hack and checking their systems to figure out whether they could absorb or manage similar threats.

Reuters’ report also noted that a cybersecurity team at one of the largest US banks contacted Binance within hours of the hack. A Binance spokesperson confirmed with Cointelegraph that the exchange shared its publicly released incident report with all its banking partners and was not aware of any vulnerabilities affecting them.

Muehlbauer explained the procedure currently unfolding is “how a maturing framework should work.” He added that “it’s not a signal that regulators are pulling back from the industry.”

The inquiries also come after the Federal Reserve removed a requirement in April 2025 for state member banks to notify regulators before engaging in crypto activities. The Fed said it would continue overseeing those activities through its regular supervisory process.

A Federal Reserve spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the agency had nothing to share regarding the reported inquiries. Cointelegraph also contacted the OCC for comment but has not heard back at the time of publishing.

Related: Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool

The largest crypto hack raises concerns

Binance said in its Nov. 3 incident report that approximately $6.34 billion in digital assets were affected by the attack on Oct. 29, with $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted as of the report.

According to the crypto exchange, the attack began with compromised software installed by an engineer in June. Hackers later employed social engineering, stolen credentials and malicious software to get access to wallet systems and carry out unauthorized transfers.

Dr. Darren Williams, founder and CEO of cybersecurity firm BlackFog, told Cointelegraph that the methods used in the attack pose potential risks to traditional banks, particularly those offering crypto custody and payment services.

“Attackers no longer need to break encryption or steal private keys if they can compromise the trusted systems and people authorized to move money,” Williams said.

He warned that hackers could use compromised employee devices, accounts or third-party services to move money without triggering any alerts. He also said the growing use of agentic AI in financial operations could pose even more risks.

“The priority must be stopping unauthorized transactions and data exfiltration before assets or sensitive information leave the organization, not simply investigating the damage afterwards,” Williams said.

Binance has since said that it has strengthened its security controls and was bringing in independent cybersecurity experts to review the attack.

title: Europe’s largest asset manager Amundi tokenizes equity index fund on Ethereum
summary: The new share class offers blockchain-based exposure to an index tracking 600 companies across European markets.
content:
Amundi, Europe’s largest fund manager by assets, has launched a tokenized share class of its STOXX Europe 600 equity index fund on Ethereum, expanding its blockchain-based investment offerings beyond money market funds.

The new share class was issued on Ethereum in collaboration with CACEIS, a European asset-servicing company that provided the tokenization infrastructure. The fund will continue to be available through traditional investment channels, Amundi said in a Thursday announcement.

The fund tracks the STOXX Europe 600 Index, which covers 600 large-, mid- and small-cap companies across developed European markets. Amundi said it plans to develop a broader range of tokenized funds for institutional clients and digital platforms, citing potential improvements in accessibility, settlement speed and operational efficiency.

The launch follows the asset manager’s introduction of its first tokenized money market fund share class in November 2025, also developed with CACEIS on Ethereum.

Related: Robinhood’s Tenev warns US tokenization uncertainty deters ‘serious assets’

Tokenized stock market grows as US companies dominate

Amundi’s move comes amid rapid growth in the global tokenized equities market, although the largest products remain concentrated in US-related assets.

The value of tokenized stocks reached $4.24 billion as of Wednesday, Nov. 4, up nearly 27% over the past 30 days, according to RWA.xyz data. The platform’s 10 largest tokenized equity products by value were all tied to US companies or US-listed securities, including Securitize, SpaceX, Circle and Alphabet.

Tokenized equities. Source: RWA.xyz

Meanwhile, European financial firms have pressed regulators to accelerate reforms. In April, a coalition of 39 companies and industry groups warned that the EU risked falling behind the US in tokenized finance, calling for expanded asset eligibility, higher volume limits and the removal of time restrictions on licenses under the bloc’s Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) Pilot Regime.

title: Bull Bitcoin Becomes First Exchange to Add Payjoin Privacy Deposits, Withdrawals, and Payjoin-by-Default Trading
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bull Bitcoin Becomes First Exchange to Add Payjoin Privacy Deposits, Withdrawals, and Payjoin-by-Default Trading
Bull Bitcoin is the first Bitcoin exchange to offer Payjoin privacy as a deposit and withdrawal option. Every on-chain buy or sell via BULL Wallet is now a Payjoin by de...
content:
Bull Bitcoin announced deep Payjoin integration with its exchange, claiming to be the first Bitcoin exchange in the world to offer Payjoin as a deposit and withdrawal option. The update unlocks two new concepts: “Payjoin-by-default and Payjoin trading,” according to he press release shared with Bitcoin Magazine.

Founded by Francis Pouliot in Canada in 2013, Bull Bitcoin is the world’s longest-running Bitcoin-only exchange. Its non-custodial platform lets customers in Canada, Europe, and Latin America buy Bitcoin directly into their own wallet and sell Bitcoin to their bank account. Bull Bitcoin also develops BULL Wallet, a free and open-source self-custodial Bitcoin wallet. The company has been self-funded since its inception. 

Payjoin is a Bitcoin onchain privacy protocol that breaks basic assumptions made by on-chain analysis firms about user behaviour. One such assumption is that one of the unspect transaction outputs (UTXOs) resulting from a bitcoin transaction will be change returning to the sender. Or that amounts are more often than not denominated in dollars. Payjoin protocols add an off-chain coordination layer such that the amounts sent and returned to the sender obfuscate user intent and thus protect their privacy on-chain. Payjoin does not require a hard fork or a soft fork into Bitcoin consensus. Instead, it must be adopted by user wallets and exchanges to scale, but it also does not depend on collective action to benefit individual users. Bull Bitcoin’s Payjoin integration is closely based on the Payjoin Foundation‘s work.

Every time a BULL Wallet user buys or sells Bitcoin on-chain via their built-in exchange, that transaction will be a Payjoin by default. This will allow Bitcoin buyers to passively aggregate their wallet’s UTXOs, which can reduce their Bitcoin mining fees in the future. “Many Bitcoin users do not even know that they must periodically “merge” their coins by spending them to a new address in their Bitcoin wallet, if they want to reduce the economic costs of future Bitcoin transactions,” explained the press release. Payjoin-by-default automates this process. Not only does this help reduce the size of Bitcoin’s UTXO set, making it easier for everyone to run a Bitcoin node, but it also reduces fee pressure for every Bitcoin user. 

Payjoin trading is a novel concept that protects users from malicious actors trying to gain insights into their financial habits by conducting chain analysis. Because transaction amounts in Bitcoin are public, it’s possible to reverse-engineer information such as someone’s salary or trading strategies such as dollar-cost averaging. Bull Bitcoin is a non-custodial exchange, so every trade leaves an on-chain trail. 

The widespread adoption of Payjoin in the Bitcoin network makes common input ownership and change output detection heuristics less reliable. Bull Bitcoin’s Payjoin implementation reduces round numbers in the amounts sent as well as address reuse, and reduces the possibility of third-party onlookers guessing the fiat value of Bitcoin transactions. Introducing Payjoin-by-default and Payjoin trading means that the more people use Bull Bitcoin, the more privacy the Bitcoin network gains as a whole; “This is part of our philosophy to align the incentives of our company with the interests of all Bitcoin users.”

In December 2024, BULL Wallet became the world’s first Bitcoin wallet to integrate the Payjoin V2 protocol. This was a highly experimental project coordinated with Dan Gould and the Payjoin Dev Kit team, who have since founded the Payjoin Foundation. 

Researchers have used the insights from this experimentation to improve the Payjoin experience to make it more seamless and resistant to attacks. The software powering Payjoin, both for the wallet and for the exchange, is fully free and open-source. 

To benefit from these features, all a user has to do is download BULL Wallet, create a Bull Bitcoin exchange account, and log into their account via the BULL mobile app; “The rest happens automatically, like magic!”

title: South Korea Pushes 22% Crypto Tax to 2029 in Fourth Delay, Offers Three-Year Loss Carryforward
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

South Korea Pushes 22% Crypto Tax to 2029 in Fourth Delay, Offers Three-Year Loss Carryforward
South Korea's government will ask lawmakers to delay its 22% crypto gains tax to 2029 and let investors carry losses forward for up to three years.
This post South Korea Pushes 22% Crypto...
content:
South Korea’s government plans to push back its tax on cryptocurrency gains by another two years to 2029, Finance and Economy Minister Lee Hyeong-il said Thursday, in what would be the fourth delay since the levy was written into law.

The tax is scheduled to take effect in January. To postpone it, the National Assembly must amend the Income Tax Act before then, and Lee said the government would seek lawmakers’ approval during this year’s regular session.

“It weighs heavily on me to propose another delay after the tax has already been postponed three times,” Lee said at a press briefing in Seoul.

Korea legislated the tax in 2020 for a 2022 start. It was then pushed to 2023, 2025 and 2027 as officials conceded that tax systems and investor protections were not ready.

Waiting on U.S. data

The main reason for the new delay is data on overseas trading. When investors move tokens bought abroad onto a Korean exchange, the exchange may have no record of the purchase price needed to calculate a taxable gain.

That gap closes in 2029, when Korea and the United States begin exchanging information under the OECD-backed Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, or CARF. Introducing the tax before then could put Korea’s domestic crypto market at a disadvantage, the government said.

“Once we begin receiving cryptocurrency transaction data from the United States in 2029, we will have enough information to tax investors who use US exchanges on the same basis as those who trade in the domestic market,” Lee said.

The government also cited the need to align the tax with the proposed Digital Asset Act, which would set rules for digital asset businesses and strengthen investor protection. Korea’s broader crypto rulebook has been moving on several fronts, including a Bank of Korea push to write stablecoins into foreign exchange law.

Exchanges, investors and lawmakers had pressed for more time, with exchanges saying unclear reporting requirements held up system development and testing.

What the 2029 tax would look like

The rate itself is not changing. Individuals would pay 22%, including local income tax, on annual net income above 2.5 million won, or about $1,869, from selling or lending virtual assets such as bitcoin.

What is new is a proposed three-year loss carryforward. Under current law, only losses from the same year can offset gains, so an investor could owe tax in a profitable year even after losing more the year before.

Under the proposal, losses realized in 2029 could offset gains through 2032. Losses realized before the tax takes effect would not be eligible, the government said, citing the volatility of crypto prices as the reason for the change.

The carryforward would follow similar practices in the U.S. and Britain, the finance ministry said. It also said it will work with the Financial Services Commission to speed up the digital asset law.

The government plans to use the extra two years to collect overseas trading records and analyze them alongside domestic tax data. A working group of industry representatives, experts and government officials will review tax rules for different types of transactions and ways to simplify filing through the first half of 2027.

If the review finds that more legislation is needed, the government plans to submit amendments during the National Assembly’s 2027 regular session. Detailed tax guidelines are due in the first half of 2028.

For Korea’s large base of retail crypto traders, the announcement extends a tax-free window that was supposed to close in 2022. Whether 2029 holds depends on the Assembly passing the amendment in the coming weeks and on the U.S. data exchange starting on schedule.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

content:
2026-11-05T19:17:06.401+02:00

Thursday, 05/11/2026 | 17:17 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • FSCA finalises the withdrawal and expands investigation to four other financial services companies.
  • Mixirite did not oppose the withdrawal but disputed regulator’s findings of financial misconduct.

South Africa’s Financial Sector Conduct Authority has made the withdrawal of Mixirite’s financial services licence final, citing material breaches of financial sector laws and concerns over the company's treatment of clients.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The decision takes immediate effect. The FSCA said Mixirite no longer meets the fit and proper requirements to operate as a financial services provider.

The regulator provisionally withdrew the licence in June 2026 following preliminary findings from an ongoing investigation. Mixirite was given an opportunity to respond and explain why the decision should not become permanent. The company submitted its representations but did not oppose the final withdrawal, although it disagreed with the investigation findings.

FSCA Identifies Aggressive Sales Practices and Governance Failures

The FSCA found that Mixirite's agents used aggressive, manipulative and high-pressure sales techniques when dealing with clients.

The investigation also found that individuals who were not authorised representatives provided financial advice. Other concerns included promises of unrealistic or guaranteed returns and failures to conduct proper suitability and needs analyses.

The regulator also identified inadequate risk disclosures and significant governance concerns.

FSCA Expands Investigation to Four Other Companies

The FSCA has expanded its investigation to include Complyxpert, Start Stream, Rayn Investments and Advice 365, along with their key persons.

The regulator is examining possible breaches of financial services laws by the companies and their associated individuals. It did not disclose specific allegations or further details, citing the sensitivity of the matters and the need to preserve the integrity of the investigation.

The FSCA said it would provide "further updates on the investigation and any resulting decisions at the appropriate time".

title: Keel (KEEL) Sells Entire Bitcoin Treasury for $192 Million, Will Sell BTC Daily
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Keel (KEEL) Sells Entire Bitcoin Treasury for $192 Million, Will Sell BTC Daily
Keel sold 2,520 bitcoin in the third quarter, left its treasury near zero and said Quebec-mined coins will now be sold every day as it pivots to AI data centers.
This post Keel (KEEL) Sells Entire Bitco...
content:
Keel Infrastructure sold its entire bitcoin treasury in the third quarter, offloading 2,520 bitcoin for $192 million and leaving the company with only nominal holdings at Sept. 30, the former Bitfarms miner reported Thursday.

The sales covered the 2,261 bitcoin Keel held going into the quarter plus the 259 it mined, and the company said it timed them during periods of strength. Going forward, bitcoin mined from Keel’s remaining Quebec operations will be sold on a daily basis, “effectively eliminating the Company’s exposure to Bitcoin price movements on treasury holdings.”

The move completes a shift Keel began earlier this year, when the company, then still trading as Bitfarms (BITF), started selling its stack and winding down U.S. mining to fund high-performance computing and AI infrastructure.

From bitcoin miner to AI landlord

Keel Infrastructure Corp. rebranded from Bitfarms after completing a U.S. redomiciliation to Delaware in April and now describes itself as a North American digital infrastructure and energy company. Legacy bitcoin mining still shows up in the results, but the center of gravity has moved.

Revenue from continuing operations fell to $28 million from $68 million a year earlier, largely because Keel stopped U.S. bitcoin mining in the second quarter and because the average bitcoin price declined. Adjusted EBITDA swung to a negative $27 million from a positive $19 million. General and administrative expenses roughly doubled to $34 million as the company hired senior specialists and booked higher stock-based compensation. The company still posted about $780 million of unrestricted cash as of Nov. 4 and said it has no current need for debt or equity financing before signing a lease.

“Power supply is getting scarcer while demand keeps climbing,” CEO Ben Gagnon said in the release. “Keel’s 2027 and 2028 power is further advanced, more secure, and closer to delivery than it was last quarter.”

CFO Jonathan Mir added that capital deployed ahead of a lease becomes equity in project financing and that the company examines opportunities to recycle capital on an ongoing basis.

What Keel is building instead

Construction began at Moses Lake in September after Keel cleared Notice to Proceed, and the company expects it to be the first energized site generating HPC revenue in 2027. It also engineered an optional plan for next-generation Vera Rubin architecture at the site. Permitting advanced at Sharon and Panther Creek in Pennsylvania, and load studies could expand secured data center capacity from 478 MW toward nearly 1.9 GW if Panther Creek and Scrubgrass expansions proceed. Keel has also moved to consolidate older bitcoin sites into a single AI campus.

The development pipeline stands at about 2.2 gigawatts with grid interconnections already in place across Pennsylvania, Washington State and Québec. That is the inventory Keel is trying to lease before the cash from the bitcoin sale and the remaining Quebec mining runs down.

Keel is not alone. Riot Platforms and Hut 8 have sold thousands of bitcoin this year to fund AI builds and share buybacks, and Riot this week named Anthropic as the tenant on a roughly $28 billion Texas lease. Public miners that once marketed themselves as bitcoin accumulators are turning their power and land into AI capacity instead.

Keel’s remaining mining footprint sits in Quebec, where regulated power rates still support production. Those coins will no longer sit on the balance sheet. The company will sell them the day they are mined, converting hashrate into cash for the infrastructure build rather than into a treasury that moves with the bitcoin price.

The open question is whether the leases close on the terms Gagnon described before the cash pile is spent. Keel says competitive tension is high at all three near-term sites and that multiple creditworthy parties are at the table. Until a signed lease shows up, the $192 million bitcoin sale is the clearest proof that the company has left the treasury strategy behind.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Moonshot AI Eyes 8,000+ Nvidia Blackwell GPUs Through European Cloud Providers Despite US Chip Curbs
summary: Moonshot AI is exploring access to more than 8,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs in Europe as China’s AI developers seek computing power beyond domestic supply.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: NVIDIA

Moonshot AI is exploring access to more than 8,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs in Europe as China’s AI developers seek computing power beyond domestic supply.

CNBC reported on November 5 that the Beijing-based Kimi developer has discussed renting advanced GPU capacity from European cloud operators, although no agreement has been confirmed.

Moonshot AI Seeks More Nvidia Blackwell GPU Capacity

Moonshot AI has reportedly approached European neocloud providers about renting large clusters of Nvidia Blackwell GPUs to expand its computing resources. The discussions involve access to more than 8,000 processors, potentially supporting both AI inference and model training.

Moonshot AI is leasing Nvidia Blackwell GPU clusters from European data centers and cloud providers to secure advanced computing power amid US chip restrictions. Source: CNBC via X

According to CNBC, three people familiar with the discussions said the Chinese AI company has been actively pursuing additional computing capacity in Europe. One source described Moonshot’s efforts as “very aggressive” as it seeks access to Nvidia’s advanced hardware.

The proposed arrangements would allow Moonshot to use computing infrastructure physically located outside China without bringing the restricted processors into the country. Under this model, European data center operators would maintain the hardware while Moonshot would pay for remote access to its computing capacity.

The financial terms could also reflect the regulatory complications surrounding such arrangements. One source told CNBC that a proposal had called for Moonshot to pay an upfront premium of 30% to 50% above the amount charged to a non-Chinese customer. However, the discussions remain preliminary, and there is no confirmation that the company has accepted those terms or secured the capacity.

European Cloud Rentals Raise Questions About US Chip Restrictions

The discussions highlight a gap between restrictions on physical semiconductor shipments and the growing international market for cloud-based AI computing.

Washington has restricted direct exports of Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell processors to Chinese customers over national security concerns. The controls are intended to limit China’s access to high-performance computing hardware that can support advanced AI development.

Nvidia requires data center partners to reserve at least 51% of future services for non-Chinese customers to restrict remote GPU access by Chinese firms. Source: @MartiniGuyYT via X

However, renting computing capacity from an independent overseas operator presents a different regulatory question from purchasing restricted chips and transporting them into China. The customer can execute AI workloads remotely while the GPUs remain inside a data center in another country.

This distinction has become a growing concern for US policymakers. A Congressional Research Service report published in April 2026 identified remote access to advanced AI computing through cloud services as a potential weakness in existing export-control enforcement. It noted that foreign AI developers could access advanced processors through cloud providers even when direct hardware shipments were restricted.

Washington has since taken steps to clarify the rules governing overseas chip shipments. On May 31, the US Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security clarified that export license requirements also apply to advanced computing chips shipped to companies headquartered in China, even when their receiving entities operate outside the country.

A Reuters report noted that the updated guidance did not require data centers to stop using the chips or discontinue servicing existing equipment. This distinction is important because restrictions on physical exports do not automatically resolve questions surrounding remote access to independently operated computing infrastructure.

The European rental discussions therefore expose an unresolved regulatory challenge. While Washington can restrict the movement and transfer of advanced processors, controlling access to computing services hosted by independent operators in other jurisdictions presents a different enforcement task.

Previous Thailand Access Allegations Put Moonshot Under Scrutiny

Moonshot’s reported European expansion follows an earlier controversy involving Nvidia’s Blackwell hardware in Southeast Asia.

In July 2026, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios accused the Chinese AI developer of obtaining access to restricted Nvidia processors through facilities in Thailand. The allegation emerged following the release of Moonshot’s Kimi K3 model, which attracted attention for its performance against advanced US AI systems.

U.S. export controls restrict direct Blackwell chip shipments to China but permit overseas cloud rentals, despite previous White House allegations that Moonshot used a Thailand-based data center. Source: @wallstengine via X

Kratsios said the company had “acquired GB300-equipped servers and has accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its AI models.”

The GB300 is part of Nvidia’s Blackwell generation. The White House’s remarks raised questions about how Chinese AI developers could obtain access to advanced American processors through overseas infrastructure despite Washington’s export restrictions.

The allegation also increased attention on the role of third-party data center operators and international computing providers in the AI hardware supply chain.

Moonshot did not publicly confirm the reported Thailand arrangement in response to the earlier allegations. The latest European discussions indicate that access to overseas computing infrastructure remains an important part of the company’s reported capacity expansion efforts.

Kimi’s Growing Demand Increases Computing Requirements

Moonshot’s interest in additional Nvidia hardware comes as the company expands its AI model development and commercial services.

The startup launched Kimi K3 in July 2026, describing it as a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model designed for advanced reasoning, coding, and knowledge-intensive tasks. Moonshot said the model delivered performance approaching Anthropic’s Fable system, placing its latest release in direct competition with advanced models developed by US technology companies.

The launch also exposed pressure on the company’s existing computing infrastructure. Following a surge in demand, Moonshot temporarily paused new subscriptions to Kimi K3 to prioritize computing resources for existing users.

In a July announcement, the company acknowledged the capacity challenge, stating: “We’re adding capacity as fast as we can and will reopen new subscription spots in batches.”

The situation illustrates why additional inference capacity could be particularly important. Training requires substantial computing resources to develop and improve models, while inference relies on GPUs to process user requests and generate responses after deployment. Growing adoption can therefore increase infrastructure requirements even after a model has completed its initial training.

Moonshot has also been linked to other Nvidia computing arrangements. A July 2026 report by Bloomberg, cited by Reuters, said the company had access to approximately 20,000 Nvidia chips through an agreement with Alibaba. Those processors were reported to belong to Nvidia’s older Hopper generation, although Alibaba disputed claims that it had supplied H200 chips.

The reported discussions with European neocloud operators represent a separate potential source of access to newer Blackwell infrastructure. They could help Moonshot expand its computing resources for both model development and serving users, although the scale of any eventual arrangement remains unknown.

For Nvidia, the reported interest highlights continued demand for its advanced processors across international AI markets, including from developers facing restrictions on direct access to the hardware.

Whether Moonshot secures the proposed European capacity will depend on commercial negotiations, infrastructure availability and the regulatory requirements governing remote access. For now, the discussions offer another indication that competition for advanced AI computing is extending beyond traditional hardware purchases into a global market for rented GPU capacity.

content:

  • The firm's CEO and CFO bought 80,000 shares weeks before the cancellation.
  • The company's voting share capital now stands at 337 million shares, with no shares held in treasury.

IG Group Holdings has cancelled 24,522,153 ordinary shares held in its treasury account, reducing its issued share capital to 337,035,715 shares.

The cancellation took place on 5 November 2026, according to a regulatory announcement issued under UK Listing Rule.

title: U.S.-Sanctioned Moscow Exchange Will List Bitcoin on Dec. 1 as Russia Pulls Crypto Trading Home
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S.-Sanctioned Moscow Exchange Will List Bitcoin on Dec. 1 as Russia Pulls Crypto Trading Home
Russia's largest exchange, Moscow Exchange,. will open bitcoin trading on Dec. 1 under the country's new crypto law, with retail buyers tested and capped at 300,000 rubles a year.
This p...
content:
Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest trading venue, will begin trading bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT on Dec. 1, the exchange announced this week, calling it the country’s first organized market for digital currencies.

The launch puts bitcoin on the same screens Russians use to trade Sberbank and Gazprom shares. It also puts a major crypto venue inside an institution that sits under U.S. sanctions. The first phase will run as a pilot. Participants will connect as they are ready, and the exchange said interest has come from existing members, their clients and businesses that already use digital currencies for investment and settlement.

How the Moscow market will work

Trading will run on the exchange’s existing stock market technology and follow its stock market hours, from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time, the exchange told Russian newspaper Vedomosti. The National Clearing Centre, the exchange’s clearing arm, will clear every trade.

From day one, clients can settle trades the same day or the next day, and the exchange will offer swaps to help participants manage liquidity. BTC, ETH and USDT will trade in both addressed and addressless modes, and the list is set to grow over time with Russian and international instruments.

Custody will run through partner digital depositaries, a new type of entity created under the country’s rules. A Moscow Exchange executive first previewed the plan on Oct. 31.

Retail access is tight. Non-qualified investors must pass a test before they can buy, and they can purchase no more than 300,000 rubles of digital currency a year, roughly $3,700, through a single broker. Qualified investors face no cap. The exchange had first flagged plans to debut bitcoin trading in October.

For the exchange, the structure keeps crypto inside a regime it already runs. Brokers connect the way they do for equities, trades net through the same clearing system and investor classifications carry over from the stock market. That lowers the barrier for banks and brokerages that want to offer bitcoin without building separate custody and matching systems of their own.

Sanctions loom over USDT

The U.S. Treasury blocked Moscow Exchange and the National Clearing Centre in June 2024 as part of a broader push against Russia’s financial system over the war in Ukraine. That makes the clearing house holding customers’ USDT a sanctioned entity.

Tether routinely freezes wallets tied to addresses on the Treasury’s sanctions list, which raises questions about how the stablecoin issuer would treat USDT held through the Moscow clearing structure. Neither the exchange nor Tether has publicly addressed that issue.

The choice of USDT, a dollar-pegged token, is notable for a market built in part to operate outside the dollar system. Bitcoin and ether carry no issuer that can freeze balances.

Pulling offshore activity home

The market rests on Federal Law No. 282-FZ, “On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights,” whose main provisions took effect on Sept. 1. The law still bans using crypto for domestic payments, though exporters and importers can use it to settle cross-border trade.

Russian officials have spent the past year building the plumbing. Lawmakers handed securities regulators oversight of crypto last month, and the central bank licensed Sberbank for crypto work weeks earlier.

The goal is to move trading that Russians already do on offshore exchanges and peer-to-peer desks onto domestic, supervised rails where the state can see it and tax it. Moscow is betting that a familiar exchange, tied to brokers that Russian investors already use, can pull that volume back.

The open question is whether the caps and testing keep retail traders offshore, and whether foreign liquidity will touch a sanctioned venue at all. For now, Russia’s first organized bitcoin market opens on Dec. 1, with a pilot and a modest ceiling.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Binance Reveals How Hackers Moved $6.34B After Breaching Its Wallet-Signing System
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance claimed that their $6.34 billion hack happened over a month-long attack campaign. Hackers’ applications included fake job interviews, malware and using compromised internal AI tooling. Around $2.85
The post Binance Reveals How Hackers Moved $6.34B After Breaching Its Wallet-Si...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance claimed that their $6.34 billion hack happened over a month-long attack campaign.
  • Hackers’ applications included fake job interviews, malware and using compromised internal AI tooling.
  • Around $2.85 billion in funds has been frozen, with 98% of affected tokens being topped up.

Binance has released its first detailed account of the October 29th breach, revealing that attackers spent months building access before reaching the exchange’s wallet-signing infrastructure.

https://t.co/sU9dUqLQDH

— Binance (@binance) November 3, 2026

Social engineering, endpoint compromise and the misuse of the Ethereum transaction authorization capabilities were all cited by the crypto exchange as causatives in the incident.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

  • Binance Hack Started Months Before the $6.34B Theft
  • Internal AI Tool Became Part of the Attack Path
    • Attackers Exploited EIP-7702 to Keep Moving Crypto
    • Binance Freezes $2.85B and Replenishes 98% of Tokens

Binance Hack Started Months Before the $6.34B Theft

Binance says the hack started back in June, when a newly hired Wallet DevOps engineer downloaded a modified software package during the installation of an AI coding tool.

Binance noticed that incident and rotated credentials and replaced the device. But the attacker had already learned information about how the engineer worked on wallet infrastructure and its other team members. Walls was targeted again in September using a legitimate job-search website.

The attacker pretended to be a recruiter, followed by a video interview, and then requested the engineer’s attention to download a coding assignment. Malware in the repository was used to run during installation and write to the employee’s work computer.

Read More: Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B

Internal AI Tool Became Part of the Attack Path

The attackers were then able to use the impersonated device and AI tool to gain access into the systems of two other engineers, Binance said.

By October 20th, they found a token for container deployments in a Wallet DevOps employee’s possession. A stolen set of credentials was leveraged to launch a container and send malicious code into Binance’s wallet environment on October 29th.

The hackers subsequently accessed an internal wallet-signing service, thus circumventing the exchange’s typical withdrawal procedure.

Attackers Exploited EIP-7702 to Keep Moving Crypto

Several networks were vulnerable to the hack. The attacker has received 5 Binance hot wallets with a total of 233.46 million XRP. Other wallets made another 970,503 SOL and 44.2 million OP transfers, followed by 18,270 BTC transfers.

EIP-7702 is a feature in Ethereum that enables delegation of execution rights from an account to a smart contract, which the attackers exploited.

According to Binance, their research was able to detect a malicious nonce manipulation using 50 signing transactions. They were never removed after the withdrawals were paused and withdrawing was not an option to stop all transfers instantly.

Also, the Multi-Party Computation wallet setup made it more difficult since there was no single private key to take out the malicious authorizations at a speedy go.

Binance Freezes $2.85B and Replenishes 98% of Tokens

Around $6.34 billion in digital assets were affected, according to Binance co-CEO Richard Teng. According to the CEO, more than $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted with assistance from the law enforcement and the tokens’ issuers and blockchain intelligence companies.

On 29 October, Binance was the target of one of the most sophisticated attacks the digital asset industry has ever seen. ~$6.34B in assets were impacted. We take full responsibility and we’re making it right.

No user bears the loss. We set aside more than the full amount required. At this moment, 98% of impacted tokens had been replenished; we’re completing the remaining 2%. Withdrawals have broadly resumed.

This wasn’t one mistake or one breach – it was a months-long campaign. We’re publishing the full report because the lessons go far beyond Binance.

~$2.85B has already been frozen or intercepted with law enforcement, issuers and blockchain intelligence firms. The speed of coordination could not be matched in traditional finance.

— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) November 3, 2026

Binance has pledged to take the hit, not the buyers. By October 31st, token assets representing 98% had been renewed, and the remainder of less liquid assets were being bought in.

The exchange has since rebuilt wallet systems and internal AI tools impacted, replaced compromised devices, revoked credentials and added AI-based behavioural anomaly detection.

title: Bitcoin Price Crashes Over 5% to $75,000 as Tech Rout Wipes Out Leveraged Longs
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Crashes Over 5% to $75,000 as Tech Rout Wipes Out Leveraged Longs
Bitcoin price fell from above $80,800 to near $76,600 on Thursday morning as a Nasdaq selloff in chip and AI stocks spilled into crypto.
This post Bitcoin Price Crashes Over 5% to $75,000 as Tech Rout W...
content:
Bitcoin price fell about 5% on Thursday morning, sliding from above $80,800 to near $76,000 as a sharp selloff in technology stocks spread into crypto and wiped out leveraged traders betting on further gains, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows.

The drop erased the rebound that had carried bitcoin back above $80,000 overnight. It touched a low near $76,100 shortly after the U.S. stock market opened, its weakest level since the start of the week.

The reversal came fast. Bitcoin held near $80,000 through Wednesday, and early Thursday traders were cheering a short squeeze that pushed it past $80,500. Within roughly two hours of the opening bell, the bitcoin price was more than $4,000 lower.

Wall Street’s AI trade breaks

The trigger sat on Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled as much as 3.9% on Thursday and slipped into correction territory, trading 10% below the record close it set last month, CNBC reported. The S&P 500 fell about 2%, erasing Wednesday’s rally, its best session in three months.

Chip and AI stocks took the worst of it. Nvidia and Broadcom each fell about 5%, Tesla lost around 9% and neocloud names CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN dropped between 9% and 13%. Qualcomm slid 9% after a weak outlook. Sandisk was down nearly 19% at the time of writing.

Investors are pricing in a Democratic-controlled Congress after Tuesday’s midterms. Traders fear new limits on the data center buildout, and UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of U.S. data center capacity additions expected in 2028 could be at risk from construction pauses, Reuters reported. The selling started in Asia, where South Korea’s Kospi closed down more than 5% as Samsung and SK hynix sank.

U.S. stocks shed $2.3 trillion in market value within the first hour of trading, with the Russell 2000 plunging 2.5% and on pace for its biggest one-day drop since June 5

Bitcoin price has traded alongside that AI-heavy tech complex for most of the year, and bitcoin miners are now part of it. Many have sold bitcoin to fund AI data centers, so the same political risk now weighs on both.

Leverage unwinds

Leverage turned the move into a flush. Roughly $370 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in about an hour as bitcoin broke $77,000 and ether fell below $2,300, most of them long bets. Wider tallies circulating on X put long liquidations closer to $400 million over the same 60 minutes.

The U.S. stock market shed more than $1 trillion in value within minutes of the open, and crypto went with it.

Wednesday’s short squeeze had pulled in late buyers with borrowed money. When stocks broke, those positions were the first to go, and forced selling pushed the bitcoin price through support around $77,000.

Hot labor data cools rate-cut hopes

The macro backdrop offered little cover. Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 last week, matching July’s level, which was the lowest since 1969, Reuters reported. Economists had expected 196,000.

A labor market that tight gives the Federal Reserve little reason to ease. That leaves risk assets leaning on growth stories like AI to carry them, and that story is now under political pressure.

Fund flows were only a small offset. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $74.6 million on Wednesday, breaking a three-day run of outflows, led by Fidelity’s FBTC while BlackRock’s IBIT saw money leave.

What comes next for bitcoin price

The next test is Friday’s October jobs report, followed by October CPI on Nov. 10 and the Fed’s Dec. 9 decision. Policy risk is building too, with House Democrats drafting their own market structure bill ahead of taking over the committees in January.

Traders are watching whether bitcoin can hold the $75,000 area, which held as support on election night and several times since August. A break would leave the bitcoin price near its lowest levels in months.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $76,200.

Micah Zimmerman

title: How Finalto Drives Innovation: Turning Market Demand into Client Solutions

He examines the interpersonal aspects of client relationships and opportunities to enhance the firm’s pro...
content:

Thursday, 05/11/2026 | 14:43 GMT by Finalto

Disclaimer

  • Finalto drives innovation by turning client demand into tailored solutions.

Brian Chong, Head of Sales, Finalto Asia, brings 18 years of financial services experience spanning online trading, institutional sales and wealth management across Sydney, London and Singapore. He examines the interpersonal aspects of client relationships and opportunities to enhance the firm’s products and services.

At Finalto, innovation is not viewed as a one-off achievement. It is a structured process that transforms market insights into practical solutions designed to solve real client challenges.

Our experience has shown that successful innovation rarely happens by chance. Instead, it begins with a systematic approach that identifies client needs, brings together expertise from across the business, and turns market opportunities into practical solutions.

1. Planning Innovation to Identify Latent Market Demand

Innovative ideas should carefully emerge from the study of a company’s processes, identified inefficiencies, missed opportunities or as the result of a deep familiarity with the market that triggers a gap that can be filled with a new technology or product.

A good example comes from Finalto Asia, where growing demand for local-currency-denominated gold products highlighted an opportunity to better serve regional market participants.

Clients in that market want more flexibility in gold pricing. Once this market feedback was shared with our product and development teams, work began on creating a solution tailored to those requirements.

This insight led to the development of Finalto’s suite of gold products, which enables clients to access them in grams, taels, ounces, and various local currencies, accommodating diverse local preferences and trading practices across Asia. In other words: we engineered a solution tailored to local trading hours, liquidity needs, and regulatory conditions in Asia.

In the words of Brian Chong, Head of Sales, Finalto Asia: “The most valuable innovations come from solving real client problems. Our gold offering was developed after listening to clients across Asia and understanding where existing market solutions fell short. By building around those requirements, we’ve created a product that gives clients greater choice, more relevant market access, and the confidence to pursue new opportunities as demand for precious metals continues to grow.”

2. Connecting Global and Regional Teams

The gold product example also highlights another important source of innovation: the interaction between local insight and global capability.

Finalto Asia is part of a broader global business, drawing on international talent and global infrastructure. We take into consideration the demands, preferences and evolving market conditions of our regional clients.

Balancing global scale with local expertise is an everyday task. The real differentiator is how effectively those perspectives are connected. That means feeding local market intelligence back to global development teams and strategic leaders, while also making full use of global resources and adapting available tools and capabilities to regional needs. The most effective innovations are often the result of collaboration, where diverse perspectives and expertise come together to solve a common challenge.

3. Educate and Engage Clients

The new products need to be understood, and their value proposition clearly established. Although this is primarily a marketing function, it goes well beyond doing just promotion. Clients need considerable engagement and training to appreciate how a new solution will effectively support their business and overcome challenges.

For liquidity providers, this means helping clients understand how new instruments work, where they create value and how they can be integrated into existing trading strategies. Adoption is often driven as much by trust and understanding as by technology itself.

4.Success Takes Time

Innovation is rarely an overnight success. For instance, in our experience with gold products we have noticed how a new development often requires a long-term process. New products often require continuous refinement, ongoing client education, and close collaboration with users to ensure they deliver lasting value.

The launch of an innovative solution is therefore not the end of the process. In many cases, it is only the beginning.

Achieving Stability Through Change

In today’s financial markets, innovation is not defined by how quickly new products are launched, but by how effectively firms identify emerging client needs and transform them into practical solutions.

The evolution of Finalto’s gold offering demonstrates that successful innovation is rarely accidental. It stems from listening closely to clients, connecting regional expertise with global resources, communicating value clearly and maintaining a long-term commitment to product development.

As market conditions continue to evolve, this disciplined approach to innovation remains one of the most effective ways to create lasting client value.

As a long-term partner, Finalto wants to ensure our products keep pace with the rate of market changes and that we’re the right safe pair of hands in a changing world.

This insight led to the development of Finalto’s suite of gold products, which enables clients to access them in grams, taels, ounces, and various local currencies, accommodating diverse local preferences and trading practices across Asia. In other words: we engineered a solution tailored to local trading hours, liquidity needs, and regulatory conditions in Asia.

In the words of Brian Chong, Head of Sales, Finalto Asia: “The most valuable innovations come from solving real client problems. Our gold offering was developed after listening to clients across Asia and understanding where existing market solutions fell short. By building around those requirements, we’ve created a product that gives clients greater choice, more relevant market access, and the confidence to pursue new opportunities as demand for precious metals continues to grow.”

2. Connecting Global and Regional Teams

The gold product example also highlights another important source of innovation: the interaction between local insight and global capability.

Finalto Asia is part of a broader global business, drawing on international talent and global infrastructure. We take into consideration the demands, preferences and evolving market conditions of our regional clients.

Balancing global scale with local expertise is an everyday task. The real differentiator is how effectively those perspectives are connected. That means feeding local market intelligence back to global development teams and strategic leaders, while also making full use of global resources and adapting available tools and capabilities to regional needs. The most effective innovations are often the result of collaboration, where diverse perspectives and expertise come together to solve a common challenge.

3. Educate and Engage Clients

The new products need to be understood, and their value proposition clearly established. Although this is primarily a marketing function, it goes well beyond doing just promotion. Clients need considerable engagement and training to appreciate how a new solution will effectively support their business and overcome challenges.

For liquidity providers, this means helping clients understand how new instruments work, where they create value and how they can be integrated into existing trading strategies. Adoption is often driven as much by trust and understanding as by technology itself.

4.Success Takes Time

Innovation is rarely an overnight success. For instance, in our experience with gold products we have noticed how a new development often requires a long-term process. New products often require continuous refinement, ongoing client education, and close collaboration with users to ensure they deliver lasting value.

The launch of an innovative solution is therefore not the end of the process. In many cases, it is only the beginning.

Achieving Stability Through Change

In today’s financial markets, innovation is not defined by how quickly new products are launched, but by how effectively firms identify emerging client needs and transform them into practical solutions.

The evolution of Finalto’s gold offering demonstrates that successful innovation is rarely accidental. It stems from listening closely to clients, connecting regional expertise with global resources, communicating value clearly and maintaining a long-term commitment to product development.

As market conditions continue to evolve, this disciplined approach to innovation remains one of the most effective ways to create lasting client value.

As a long-term partner, Finalto wants to ensure our products keep pace with the rate of market changes and that we’re the right safe pair of hands in a changing world.

title: BGC Group's Quarterly Profit More Than Doubles on Record Revenue and Fanatics Sale
summary:
BGC Group's third-quarter net income more than doubled, the New York-based interdealer broker said today (Thursday). Record revenue and a one-off gain from selling two prediction-market units to Fanatics both lifted the result.
Net income for fully diluted shares rose to $68.7 million from $26.8 mil...
content:
2026-11-05T15:39:48.129+02:00

Thursday, 05/11/2026 | 13:39 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Sales rose 13% to $832.6 million, and selling two units to Fanatics added a $35 million gain.
  • Its currency venue FMX FX grew volumes 43%, about twice the pace of the larger Cboe FX.

BGC Group's third-quarter net income more than doubled, the New York-based interdealer broker said today (Thursday). Record revenue and a one-off gain from selling two prediction-market units to Fanatics both lifted the result.

Net income for fully diluted shares rose to $68.7 million from $26.8 million a year earlier, including a $35.0 million gain on the sale of Water Street Labs and CX Clearinghouse to Fanatics.

Revenues climbed 13.0% to $832.6 million in the three months to September 30, which the company called a third-quarter record.

Currency trading was among the faster-growing lines. Foreign exchange brokerage revenue rose 13.9% to $121.5 million, and average daily volume on FMX FX, BGC's electronic currency venue, jumped 43% to $18.7 billion, according to the company.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Smallest Venue, Fastest Growth

Set against the institutional FX platforms that publish monthly volumes, FMX FX is still the smallest, but it grew the fastest in the quarter.

Cboe FX averaged $56.8 billion a day in July to September, up 21.4% from a year earlier, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation from the venue's data.

Euronext FX averaged $30.3 billion, up 26.1%, and 360T handled $40.1 billion a day, figures that FinanceMagnates.com tracks in its monthly volume reports.

FMX FX's 43% growth was about twice Cboe FX's pace, though its volume was about a third of Cboe's. BGC said spot FX and non-deliverable forwards drove the gain. FM Intelligence's Ask FMIQ answers questions on trading volumes and market data.

BGC tied the wider FX revenue increase to emerging markets, G10 forwards and its Macro Hive business. Co-Chief Executive Officer John Abularrage pointed to BGC's technology bets, "from our first fully AI-brokered institutional trade to our prediction markets partnership with Fanatics."

Treasury Futures Drive FMX

FMX, the venue BGC built with backing from a group of global banks, raised revenue by more than 35% to $30.5 million.

Its US Treasury cash platform averaged $83.0 billion a day, up 40%, and its share of the central limit order book market rose to 42% from 37%, the company said, citing Coalition Greenwich data.

The FMX Futures Exchange, which won Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) approval for Treasury and SOFR futures, averaged more than 80,000 contracts a day, nearly seven times the level a year earlier.

September averaged 112,000 contracts a day after FMX listed the full Treasury futures curve in August.

Fenics, the electronic business that houses FMX, grew revenue 13.3% to $181.3 million. Its growth platforms, which include FMX, rose 39.8% to $36.2 million, faster than the 22.9% they posted in the second quarter.

Total revenues832.6736.8+13.0%
Foreign exchange revenues121.5106.7+13.9%
ECS revenues287.1241.6+18.8%
Fenics revenues181.3160.0+13.3%
GAAP net income (fully diluted)68.726.8+156.7%
Pre-tax adjusted earnings187.5155.1+20.9%
Post-tax adjusted EPS ($)0.340.29+17.2%

Energy Desk Stays the Largest

Energy, commodities and shipping, the unit expanded by the purchase of OTC Global Holdings, remained BGC's biggest line. Its revenue rose 18.8% to $287.1 million, about a third of total revenue.

Interest-rate products brought in $219.6 million, up 12.4%, and equities $77.3 million, up 28.0%. Credit was the only brokerage line to shrink, slipping 2.5% to $67.4 million on lower emerging-market and European volumes.

BGC excludes the Fanatics gain, from a deal agreed in July, from adjusted earnings, which rose 20.9% before tax to $187.5 million.

Total GAAP expenses grew 11.0% to $783.5 million. They included a $22.6 million non-cash impairment of long-lived assets and $9.9 million of charges under a cost-reduction program.

Aubin to Step Back at Year-End

JP Aubin will become vice chairman and step down as co-chief executive at the end of the year, BGC said earlier this week. He is one of the three co-CEOs who took over from Howard Lutnick in February 2025, leaving Abularrage and Sean Windeatt as co-CEOs.

For the fourth quarter, BGC forecast revenue of $805 million to $865 million, against $756.4 million a year earlier, and pre-tax adjusted earnings of $178 million to $196 million. Liquidity stood at $917.3 million at September 30.

The board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.02 per share, payable on December 9 to shareholders of record on November 25.

title: Virtu’s Q3 Revenue Jumps 40% as Market Making Powers Profit Growth
summary:
Virtu Financial reported a sharp increase in third-quarter revenue and profit, with its Market Making business driving most of the improvement. The company also announced plans to change its state of incorporation from Delaware to Texas.
Total revenue rose 39.9% year over year to $1.15 billion in th...
content:
2026-11-05T14:36:20.241+02:00

Thursday, 05/11/2026 | 12:36 GMT by Adonis Adoni

  • Revenues rose to $1.15 billion, while net income increased 89.6% to $282.5 million.
  • Virtu has also approved plans to reincorporate in Texas.

Virtu Financial reported a sharp increase in third-quarter revenue and profit, with its Market Making business driving most of the improvement. The company also announced plans to change its state of incorporation from Delaware to Texas.

Total revenue rose 39.9% year over year to $1.15 billion in the three months ended September 30, 2026, according to the company’s earnings release. Consolidated net income increased 89.6% to $282.5 million from $149.1 million a year earlier.

Net income available to common stockholders was $153.3 million, after accounting for income attributable to noncontrolling interests. The group’s GAAP net income margin widened to 24.5% from 18.1%.

Market Making Drives the Increase

Market Making revenue climbed 47.7% to $986.8 million. The segment’s adjusted net trading income, a non-GAAP measure, increased 68.2% to $578.8 million.

Execution Services posted more modest gains, with revenue rising 5.5% to $163.0 million. Adjusted net trading income in that business edged up 1.8% to $125.2 million.

Across the group, adjusted net trading income rose 50.7% to $704.0 million, while adjusted EBITDA increased 63.5% to $437.9 million. Virtu’s adjusted EBITDA margin reached 62.2%, compared with 57.3% a year earlier.

That margin uses adjusted net trading income, rather than total revenue, as its denominator. The adjusted measures should not be confused with GAAP revenue or profit.

Texas Reincorporation Planned

Virtu said its board unanimously approved the planned Texas reincorporation, which its controlling stockholder subsequently approved by written consent. The company expects to complete the move later this year without changing operations, management, strategy, assets or employee locations.

The board also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.24 per share, payable on December 15 to shareholders of record on December 1. At quarter-end, Virtu reported $1.58 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, alongside $2.55 billion in long-term debt principal.

Virtu said its board unanimously approved the planned Texas reincorporation, which its controlling stockholder subsequently approved by written consent. The company expects to complete the move later this year without changing operations, management, strategy, assets or employee locations.

The board also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.24 per share, payable on December 15 to shareholders of record on December 1. At quarter-end, Virtu reported $1.58 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, alongside $2.55 billion in long-term debt principal.

title: Signal Week (formerly Paris Blockchain Week) Returns to Paris in July 2027
summary: Paris, France, 5th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Paris, France, 5th November 2026, Chainwire

Paris, France, November 5th, 2026, Chainwire

Signal Week, formerly Paris Blockchain Week, opens 2027 Edition as Paris Becomes the Capital of Finance, AI and Robotics.

Signal Week, formerly Paris Blockchain Week, has opened its 2027 edition, which will take place on July 6–7, 2027, at the Palais des Congrès de Paris, in the same week as RAISE Summit, the world’s leading AI event, and MACHINA Summit, Europe’s leading Physical AI event.

The announcement follows a successful seventh edition in April 2026, which marked a new chapter for the event. In 2026, Paris Blockchain Week officially became Signal Week, the Institutional Summit for Digital Assets, reflecting an audience that has shifted decisively towards banks, asset managers, regulators and governments.

For one week in July, the events will bring digital assets, artificial intelligence and robotics into the same city at the same time, gathering the people building the next generation of financial infrastructure and the technologies that will run on it.

A more institutional room

Signal Week 2027 will bring together banks, financial institutions, digital asset companies, technology firms, investors, policymakers and government representatives, with major institutions such as BlackRock, J.P. Morgan, Citi, Fidelity and BNP Paribas confirming participation.

The 2027 edition is designed around the institutions now shaping digital assets, with BlackRock, J.P. Morgan, Citi, Fidelity and BNP Paribas already confirmed. Its programme will span banks and financial institutions, fintech and payments, AI and agentic finance, and the policymakers and public officials setting the rules for the sector.

The 2026 edition saw unprecedented government participation, with more than 400 attendees from the public sector. They included Laurent Nuñez, Minister of the Interior of France; Anne Le Hénanff, Minister-Delegate for AI and Digital Affairs; and Jean-Didier Berger, Deputy of the French National Assembly. Across the event, Signal Week welcomed more than 10,000 attendees from over 100 countries, with 70% at C-suite level.

In a conversation with theCUBE and NYSE Wired, Michael Amar, Co-founder of Signal Week, said, “We really want to be the place where we bridge traditional finance and digital assets. In 2019, people were making fun of us, but actually it’s where the market is, finally.”

Charlie Méraud, Co-founder of Signal Week, added, “Signal Week is where institutional finance does business in digital assets. When we launched in 2019, we had to explain blockchain and crypto. This industry needed a room for these players to connect and start actually doing business. Signal Week is this room.”

Watch the full interview here.

Curated meetings

Signal Week 2027 will also offer curated one-to-one meetings, helping attendees connect with the right people and get the most out of the event. The 2026 edition facilitated more than 53,000 meetings, resulting in a rewarding networking experience for all attendees.

The VIP Dinner at Château de Versailles

On the eve of the summit, Signal Week will host its VIP Dinner at the Château de Versailles. The 2026 dinner brought together 500+ leaders from finance, technology and government, representing $37 trillion in assets. The 2027 edition will again convene senior figures from traditional finance, digital assets and public policy.

Super Early Bird tickets now live

Super Early Bird tickets for Signal Week 2027 are available from today at the lowest price the event will be offered at, until November 25th. Tickets are available at signalweek.com/tickets.

About Signal Week

Signal Week, formerly Paris Blockchain Week, is the Institutional Summit for Digital Assets, bringing together the financial institutions, digital asset companies, investors, policymakers and technology leaders shaping on-chain finance. Since 2019, its community has grown to more than 10,000 attendees from over 100 countries, with 70% at the C-suite level.

title: IPX Plans to Bring ‘minicoin’ Payments to LINE FRIENDS Online and Offline Stores, Expanding IP Experiences Beyond Content and Merchandise
summary: Seoul, South Korea, 5th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Seoul, South Korea, 5th November 2026, Chainwire

Seoul, South Korea, November 5th, 2026, Chainwire

With phased rollout targeted for the first half of 2027, the service is expected to connect LINE FRIENDS’ online and offline commerce with the Web3 ecosystem, offering customers in Korea and abroad an additional payment option for purchasing physical products with minicoin

Digital IP entertainment company IPX (formerly LINE FRIENDS) plans to introduce a payment service using ‘minicoin’ at LINE FRIENDS online and offline stores. The service is intended to make digital asset payments a seamless extension of the fan experience, linking fans’ engagement with character IP to the point of purchase and connecting IPX’s online and offline commerce with a Web3-based digital ecosystem.

For more than a decade, IPX has brought its character IPs to life through products, content, and pop-ups, extending these experiences across online and offline channels worldwide. Building on its expertise in IP and retail, the introduction of this service presents a new digital IP commerce model that integrates digital asset payment technology into IP merchandise purchases.

Minicoin is a utility coin developed and issued by Mini Labs under an official license granted by IPX to use its globally popular ‘minini’ character IP. Its blockchain-based ecosystem seeks to transparently record activities generated through interactions between IP and fans, including creation, consumption, and transactions, and link them to registration and settlement processes.

The minicoin payment service is planned for phased rollout across LINE FRIENDS stores in Korea and abroad, with a rollout targeted for the first half of 2027. The service is expected to offer international visitors and overseas fans additional payment options. K-POP SQUARE, which opened in the heart of Seoul’s Hongdae district in June 2025, welcomed over one million visitors in its first year, approximately 80% of whom were international fans from more than 90 countries. As digital assets gain traction as payment methods worldwide, the service is expected to see strong demand.

“This service rollout marks an important step toward using digital assets to purchase physical merchandise, beyond trading and use within specific platforms,” said an IPX official. “We believe that the value of IP can grow further as it expands beyond connecting with fans through content and products to finding new ways to engage with them across the digital IP ecosystem. We will continue to explore new IP business opportunities that connect IP, fans, and commerce together in this evolving landscape.”

 About IPX (F.K.A. LINE FRIENDS)

IPX is the new corporate name of LINE FRIENDS, a global character brand that started with original characters including BROWN, CONY, and SALLY, created for use as stickers for the leading mobile messenger app LINE and its 200 million active users worldwide. IPX has announced a new business strategy that it would accelerate the global expansion of its IP businesses by diversifying its IP portfolios targeting all ages and advancing its digital and retail business. IPX provides diverse IP experiences including BT21(BTS), ZO&FRIENDS(G-DRAGON), minini, and JOGUMAN. It has also carried out its IP-based business by partnering with global companies including Netflix (original animated series) and HoYoverse (Genshin Impact) to win the hearts of over 50 million Millennials and Generation Z worldwide. IPX currently operates in 18 markets worldwide, including Seoul, New York, LA, Tokyo, and Shanghai, and operates on 8 online sales platforms.

Since the start of Q4, crypto markets have remained volatile and continued to weaken, with major assets retreating from their highs and market participants becoming more cautious. Against this backdrop, HTX Earn recently launched an APY Boost Promotion as part of the HTX Winter Campaign. The promotion offers APY boosts on 7-day Fixed products available on HTX Earn for seven assets, with APYs of up to 10%. It aims to provide users with a relatively stable way to earn returns amid a market downturn.

Event details: https://www.htx.net.ht/en-us/support/85047689167878/

APY Boosts Available on Both Major Cryptos and Stablecoins

Assets eligible for APY boosts in this promotion include three major cryptocurrencies—BTC, ETH, and TRX—and four stablecoins—USDT, USDC, USDS, and USDD. The promotion is designed to reach a broader range of users. Long-term holders of BTC, ETH, and TRX can earn interest in their respective assets after subscribing, without selling or converting their holdings. They can keep their existing positions while earning returns.  The stablecoin selection includes widely recognized and heavily used assets, giving users more options.

Quota Limit for Boosted APY: Up to $14 Million per User

Each user can subscribe up to $2 million worth of each asset in it’s respective 7-day Fixed product. By subscribing to all seven assets, a user can access a combined quota limit for boosted APY of up to approximately $14 million. The generous subscription quota accommodates the allocation needs of users with large holdings, while the near-zero minimum subscription requirement allows users with smaller balances to participate with ease.

Repeat Subscriptions Available Upon Maturity

Interest starts accruing on the day after subscription (T+1). On the day after maturity, the principal and interest are automatically credited back to the account. The APY boost is not limited to a single 7-day term; users can subscribe again after maturity. The relatively short term also helps keep funds liquid, allowing users to decide whether to subscribe again or adjust their positions based on market conditions. Users can participate by logging in to HTX on the website or app and navigating to the Earn page.

The crypto industry remains in a cyclical adjustment phase. Against this backdrop, HTX is offering APY boosts across multiple assets with generous quota limits, aiming to deliver tangible benefits to users and stand by them through the crypto winter. Putting users first has always been a core principle at HTX. The platform will continue to focus on users’ needs and offer more promotions and benefits, including APY boost campaigns on HTX Earn.

Founded in 2013, HTX has evolved from a virtual asset exchange into a comprehensive ecosystem of blockchain businesses that span digital asset trading, derivatives, research, investments, incubation, and other businesses.

Guided by its vision to “Achieve Financial Freedom for 8 Billion People Worldwide,” HTX works to make the digital asset space more accessible to a broader audience. The platform continues to develop its products and services in response to user needs and an evolving industry landscape.

title: ACI Worldwide Lifts Earnings Outlook Despite a 12% Drop in Quarterly Revenue
summary:
ACI Worldwide said today (Thursday) that third-quarter revenue fell 12% year over year to $427 million. The payments software maker blamed the timing of license renewals, which this year fall mostly in the final quarter.
It still lifted its 2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast to $550 million to $565 milli...
content:
2026-11-05T13:40:12.914+02:00

Thursday, 05/11/2026 | 11:40 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The payments software maker said license renewals have shifted toward year-end.
  • Guidance implies close to half of this year’s adjusted EBITDA will come in the final three months.

ACI Worldwide said today (Thursday) that third-quarter revenue fell 12% year over year to $427 million. The payments software maker blamed the timing of license renewals, which this year fall mostly in the final quarter.

It still lifted its 2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast to $550 million to $565 million, from $545 million to $560 million, the third increase this year.

The guidance now leans heavily on a single quarter. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $612 million to $642 million, up 27% to 33% from $481.6 million a year earlier.

That equals about a third of ACI Worldwide's unchanged full-year revenue range of $1.895 billion to $1.925 billion, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation.

ACI set its first 2026 EBITDA range, $530 million to $550 million, in February. Adyen moved the other way last week, when it cut its 2026 EBITDA margin target to 50% and dropped its goal for 2028.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Nearly Half of the Year's EBITDA Falls in One Quarter

ACI's sales have leaned toward the end of the year before, though not this far. The fourth quarter brought 27% of annual revenue in 2025 and 28% in 2024, based on the company's results, against the 32% to 33% now implied for 2026.

The tilt is steeper in earnings. Fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA guidance of $257 million to $272 million would equal 47% to 48% of the full-year range, compared with 32% in 2025 and 34% in 2024, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation.

"With high visibility into scheduled renewals, we are confident in our full-year outlook," Chief Executive Thomas Warsop said in the earnings release.

Some of ACI's contracts run for a decade, such as the 10-year deal Arab Financial Services, a processor owned by 37 banks, signed in 2024. License revenue, the line most exposed to the timing of such renewals, fell 41% to $94.8 million from $162 million.

Third-quarter revenue still landed at the top of ACI's own $417 million to $427 million forecast, and adjusted EBITDA of $97.5 million beat its $90 million to $95 million range. Adjusted EBITDA fell 43% from a year earlier, and net income dropped to $32.5 million from $91.3 million.

$ millionQ3 2026Q3 2025Change
Revenue426.8482.4-12%
Recurring revenue309.3298.3+4%
License revenue94.8162.0-41%
Adjusted EBITDA97.5170.6-43%
Net income32.591.3-64%
New ARR bookings23.612.6+86%

Connetic Gets Its First Live Customer

ACI is moving customers onto newer software. A first client went live on ACI Connetic, its cloud payments platform, in the quarter, two more signed up, and ACI bought card switching developer Cranium Ventures to extend Connetic for Cards.

On October 27, ACI and Circle said they would test settlement in the USDC stablecoin through Connetic, starting in Colombia. ACI built the central infrastructure there for Bre-B, the instant payments scheme that launched in 2025 with mandated interoperability.

Bank software vendors have added the token before. Finastra connected its Global PAYplus hub to USDC settlement in August 2025, letting banks settle in the stablecoin while payment instructions stay in fiat currency.

Recurring Revenue Grows as New Bookings Pick Up

The segment figures show where the shortfall sat. It came from Payment Software, the unit that sells to banks and to merchant processors such as Worldpay, which renewed its use of ACI's real-time payments software in 2024.

The unit's revenue fell 24% from a year earlier to $216 million, and its net adjusted EBITDA margin narrowed to 49% from 64%. ACI said it still expects upper-single-digit growth in Payment Software for 2026.

The Biller segment, which handles consumer bill payments, grew revenue 6% year over year to $210 million. Recurring revenue, made up of software-as-a-service and maintenance fees, rose 4% to $309 million.

New annual recurring revenue bookings rose 86% from a year earlier to $24 million. New license and services bookings fell 21% to $64 million, and over the trailing 12 months annual recurring revenue bookings were down 3% at $79 million.

Operating cash flow rose 26% to $254 million in the first nine months. ACI spent $157 million buying back 3.4 million shares over that period, at an average price of $45.69, and ended September with $219 million in cash and $821 million of debt.

The unit's revenue fell 24% from a year earlier to $216 million, and its net adjusted EBITDA margin narrowed to 49% from 64%. ACI said it still expects upper-single-digit growth in Payment Software for 2026.

The Biller segment, which handles consumer bill payments, grew revenue 6% year over year to $210 million. Recurring revenue, made up of software-as-a-service and maintenance fees, rose 4% to $309 million.

New annual recurring revenue bookings rose 86% from a year earlier to $24 million. New license and services bookings fell 21% to $64 million, and over the trailing 12 months annual recurring revenue bookings were down 3% at $79 million.

Operating cash flow rose 26% to $254 million in the first nine months. ACI spent $157 million buying back 3.4 million shares over that period, at an average price of $45.69, and ended September with $219 million in cash and $821 million of debt.
