title: Malta Outscores Cyprus on AI Skills, but Trading Firms Still Hire in Cyprus
summary:

content:
2026-11-05T13:24:52.329+02:00

Thursday, 05/11/2026 | 11:24 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The Ayre Index and EU statistics both rank the smaller island ahead on digital skills and AI use.
  • Brokers and crypto exchanges listed 218 open roles in Cyprus on October 1, while Malta missed the top ten.

Malta ranks second of 56 Commonwealth members on youth readiness for artificial intelligence and Cyprus seventh, a new index shows. Online trading firms still post more jobs in Cyprus than anywhere else, an FM Intelligence analysis published today (Thursday) found.

The gap matters to an industry whose job ads increasingly ask for those skills. Of 2,557 open roles at 77 brokers, crypto exchanges and prop firms on October 1, 23% asked for AI skills, up from 19% a quarter earlier, according to consultancy FYI.LTD.

AI has also come up when brokers cut staff. IronFX cut about 150 jobs in March for efficiency amid the AI wave, according to people familiar with the matter.

The Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC ) register still held 1,966 active licenses on November 5, FM Intelligence's license monitor shows, the fourth-largest of the 10 registers it tracks.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Cyprus Still Tops the Job Ads, by a Thinner Margin

The hiring data cut the other way, though less firmly than a year ago. Cyprus held 22.8% of vacancies at the 50 largest brokers in the first quarter, FinanceMagnates.com reported in February.

On FYI's wider sample, its share was 8.5% in the fourth quarter, down from 11.1% in the third. Its 218 roles still put it ahead of the United States with 190 and Singapore with 182. Malta did not make the top ten.

Several of the island's largest employers posted fewer roles. XM went from 62 Cyprus ads to 47 and Exness from 32 to 18, while Kraken became one of the island's biggest hirers this year.

Groups split the decision in different ways. Equiti opened a technology hub in Bangalore in July, while Deriv in 2024 added a second Cyprus office in Nicosia for AI and data roles.

The headline count also flatters Cyprus. Some 38% of its ads had already run in an earlier quarter, and 25 had been open for six months or more. Counting only fresh ads, the United States comes first, by FM Intelligence's calculation.

Official Statistics Back the Ranking

The Ayre Index, published by the Ayre Think Tank, scores members on seven pillars, from access to technology to the quality of work open to young people. Malta scored 75.0 out of 100 and Cyprus 67.4, with the widest gaps in decent work and digital capability, the analysis found.

The index is a first edition, and an AI model scored its indicators. The European Commission's figures for people aged 16 to 74 point the same way.

In Malta, 66.8% of people have at least basic digital skills, against 55.8% in Cyprus and an EU average of 60.4%. Maltese enterprises use AI at more than twice the Cypriot rate, 21.5% against 9.3%.

Engineer Pay Falls Below the Top Tax Break

FinTop Consulting puts MT5 and cTrader platform engineers in Cyprus at $39,000 to almost $65,000 a year. Most of that range falls short of the salary threshold for the island's largest income tax relief for newcomers.

The full FM Intelligence analysis shows how Cyprus has filled its technology jobs since 2019, how payrolls and income per employee at CySEC-licensed firms moved between 2020 and 2025, and how many staff those firms are likely to employ at the end of 2026.

title: Circle’s $182M ARC Token Sale Drives Q3 Growth While USDC Onchain Volume Hits $13.9T
summary:
Key Takeaways: Circle raised an additional $182 million in the ARC token presale during Q3. Onchain transaction volume rose almost 50% YoY for USDC to $13.9 trillion. Reserve income dropped
The post Circle’s $182M ARC Token Sale Drives Q3 Growth While USDC Onchain Volume Hits $13.9T appeared first o...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Circle raised an additional $182 million in the ARC token presale during Q3.
  • Onchain transaction volume rose almost 50% YoY for USDC to $13.9 trillion.
  • Reserve income dropped by 8% and USDC share closed the quarter at 27%.

The results of Circle in the third quarter indicate that the business is becoming less reliant on reserve income. The stablecoin issuer reported being confident with the top line and the bottom line as the ARC token presale boosted revenues and USDC further onchained.

  • ARC Token Adds $182M to Circle’s Revenue Mix
  • Arc Expands Beyond Circle’s Stablecoin Business
    • USDC Volume Jumps to $13.9T
    • Reserve Income Slips Despite Higher USDC Circulation

ARC Token Adds $182M to Circle’s Revenue Mix

Circle reports total revenue and a reserve income of $865 million in Q3 2026, compared to 17% growth a year ago. Much of that increase was attributable to other revenues, which rose an impressive 627% to $207 million. One of the figures allocated to the ARC token presale is $182 million.

Net income from continuing operations increased five percent from the prior-year level to $226 million; adjusted EBITDA grew by 85 percent on the year to $317 million. Diluted earnings per share were up to $0.84 from $0.64 a year ago.

Read More: Circle Brings USDC and EURC Into SAP Workflows Powering 84% of Global Commerce

Arc Expands Beyond Circle’s Stablecoin Business

Arc launched on public mainnet on Sept. 16 with more than 100 institutional and ecosystem builders. Circle also released the initial 10 billion tokens of ARC. Security, usefulness and governance are the main features of the token as Arc moves towards a proof-of-stake format in 2027.

The token sale provides Circle with additional income streams involving USDC’s reserves’ traditional economics.

USDC Volume Jumps to $13.9T

Despite the weakened economic conditions of the reserve business, the activity of USDC continued to be fairly good. Average circulation for USDC during the quarter was $73.3 billion, increasing 8% over a year ago. The volume of transactions increased by 49%, reaching $13.9 trillion onchain.

At the end of the quarter, USDC had $73.9 billion worth of currency in circulation. Similarly, onchain wallet addresses with more than $10 in USDC on their wallet increased 16% in a year to 7.3 million, Circle reported.

The company, however, lost 183 bps from a year ago to 27% of the market in fiat-based stablecoins.

Read More: Circle Targets 100+ Markets and $25B Flows in Major USDC Payments Expansion Deal

Reserve Income Slips Despite Higher USDC Circulation

Circle’s reserves decreased $8 million to $658M. The largest pressure was from the reserve return rate, which fell 61 basis points to 3.5%. That was tempered a bit by a rise in circulation of the USDC.

The effect of distribution, transaction and other costs decreased by 8% to $412 million, which helped Revenue less Distribution costs total $453 million.

Circle adopted a multi-years target to increase the circulation of USDC at a compound annual rate of 40% through market cycles. It also impacted other revenues in 2026 with a guidance of $310 million to $330 million, which encompasses amounts from recognized ARC token presale revenue.

title: ApeChain Shifts APE and USDC to Chainlink CCIP Across Yuga Labs’ Cross-Chain Ecosystem

Key Takeaways: ApeChain is transitioning its cross-chain technical infrastructure from LayerZero to Chainlink CCIP. APE, USDC and other significant assets will be transferred to Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard. The
The post ApeChain Shifts APE and USDC to Chainlink CCIP Across Yuga Labs...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • ApeChain is transitioning its cross-chain technical infrastructure from LayerZero to Chainlink CCIP.
  • APE, USDC and other significant assets will be transferred to Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard.
  • The upgrade will be rolled out for the wider Yuga Labs ecosystem such as Bored Ape Yacht Club use cases.

ApeChain is revamping its cross-chain capabilities to adopt Chainlink CCIP as the universal standard for cross-chain transfers. The update includes all major tokens on APEChain such as APE, USDC and will be used to establish an identical interoperable layer throughout the Yuga Labs ecosystem.

NEW: ApeChain is deprecating its legacy cross-chain solution & migrating to Chainlink CCIP.

CCIP is now becoming the canonical cross-chain infra across the entire Yuga Labs ecosystem, starting with its flagship @BoredApeYC use cases, ApeChain, & the APE token.

Two communities. One ecosystem. One secure cross-chain standard.

— Chainlink (@chainlink) November 4, 2026

  • ApeChain Makes Chainlink CCIP Its Cross-Chain Standard
  • APE and USDC Will Become Cross-Chain Tokens
    • CCIP Gives ApeChain One Integration Layer
    • Yuga Labs Unifies Cross-Chain Infrastructure

ApeChain Makes Chainlink CCIP Its Cross-Chain Standard

ApeChain said it will migrate away from LayerZero and adopt Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol, or CCIP, as its canonical cross-chain stack. Chainlink said the rollout will extend beyond ApeChain itself, covering flagship Bored Ape Yacht Club applications and the APE token.

ApeChain is working with @chainlink to strengthen our infrastructure for the future.

We will be migrating from LayerZero to Chainlink CCIP as our canonical cross-chain stack across the @yugalabs ecosystem, including @BoredApeYC.

With CCIP as our canonical bridge, $APE, $USDC, and other key assets on ApeChain are being upgraded to a Chainlink Cross-Chain Token (CCT).

This upgrade will make it easier for dApps, communities, and their assets to connect.

— ApeCoin (@apecoin) November 4, 2026

It streamlines the cross-chain infrastructure and instead of having separate token transferring platforms throughout Yuga Labs’ ecosystems it supports them together. In the announcement, no deadline or instructions to holders of ApeChain were revealed.

APE and USDC Will Become Cross-Chain Tokens

APE, USDC, and other critical assets on ApeChain will undergo an upgrade to Chainlink Cross-Chain Tokens, or CCTs. Chainlink’s view on the CCT is a token that is programmed with the ability to send transactions over CCIP. The token developer controls the contracts, pools and cross-chain parameters of the developed tokens.

There are multiple transferring models available for CCTs such as: burn-and-mint, lock-and-mint and lock-and-unlock. This is dependent on the specific configuration of each token on supported chains. ApeChain has not mentioned yet, which model will it use for APE, USDC or other assets.

Read More: Arc Surges $1 Billion in USDC Circulating Supply

CCIP Gives ApeChain One Integration Layer

One of the main benefits of the CCT model is integration simplicity. After the token’s registration, the decentralized application or an aggregator of bridges will make contact with the CCIP router, rather than with each other separately for all the tokens.

This can facilitate dApps and communities within the Yuga Labs ecosystem to help the identical assets on several chains. The token pools also enable issuers to control cross-chain configuration, such as cross-chain transfer limits for each configuration route.

Rate limits are recommended for token pools by Chainlink to curb the amount of value that transacts down the lane over time and lower the operational exposure during an incident.

Yuga Labs Unifies Cross-Chain Infrastructure

The migration brings several Yuga Labs’ products into a common interoperability framework. For the APE and Bored Ape Yacht Club use cases, CCIP is the canonical cross-chain infrastructure for ApeChain, Chainlink explained.

The handling of ApeChain has shifted from adding another bridge to changing its current cross-chain standard to one framework that facilitates token transfer as well as application messaging.

Additionally, CCIP enables programmed token transfers where tokens and instructions are transferred among chains, for example when handling deposits, staking, and swaps. ApeChain and Chainlink have not announced the specifics of the ApeChain fee structure, nor have they come up with the final list nor timetable.

title: Ripple Expands UK Crypto Footprint With 120+ Staff and £22B Aviva Fund on XRP Ledger
summary:
Key Takeaways: Ripple now employs over 120 people on a full-time basis in its office in London. Aviva Investors released its tokenized share class of the £22 billion Sterling Liquidity
The post Ripple Expands UK Crypto Footprint With 120+ Staff and £22B Aviva Fund on XRP Ledger appeared first on Cry...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Ripple now employs over 120 people on a full-time basis in its office in London.
  • Aviva Investors released its tokenized share class of the £22 billion Sterling Liquidity Fund on XRPL.
  • Clearer UK crypto rules build better institutional involvement, says Ripple.

Ripple is solidifying its foothold in the UK while tokenization continues to grow in popularity among financial establishments on the XRP network. Now the biggest location, apart from the USA, the company operates in London, and a new XRPL institutional application is now underway in a fund launched by Aviva Investors.

  • Ripple Builds Out Its Largest International Hub
  • Ripple Secures UK Regulatory Permissions
    • £22B Aviva Fund Moves Onto XRP Ledger
    • XRPL Gains Another Institutional Tokenization Use Case

Ripple Builds Out Its Largest International Hub

The UK and Europe Managing Director, Cassie Craddock, said the UK and Europe were the early market of choice for Ripple, based on capital markets, the legal framework, regulatory knowledge and financial expertise.

Had the pleasure of joining a fireside chat at the British Residence in New York last week, on the sidelines of Swell, talking about the UK’s role in the future of financial services. TLDR: it’s going to be huge.

Not many people know that our London HQ is Ripple’s largest office hub outside of the US. We bet big on London early on. When we took on our current office in 2018 it was two floors with a lot of empty desks. Today it is three floors, every desk is full and we are over capacity.

We made that bet because the UK had the building blocks: deep capital markets, world-leading legal frameworks and regulators, and exceptional talent. But regulation was the missing piece. Post-MiCA, a gap opened up: we were signing deals with major banks across the EU while large UK institutions held back.

That has changed. The UK now has a comprehensive cryptoasset and stablecoin framework incoming, we have a superb City Minister @LucyRigby KC MP and Digital Markets Champion Christopher Woolard CBE driving this agenda forward at real pace, and we are starting to see meaningful engagement from leading financial institutions.

Last week’s announcement with @avivainvestors is a great proof point: a tokenised share class of their £22 billion Sterling Liquidity Fund, launched on the XRP Ledger.

Thanks to the British Consulate team for hosting, City of London Corporation for convening and to @citypolicychair for moderating our discussion. I’m excited for what comes next.

— Cassie Craddock (@CraddockCJ) November 4, 2026

The company opened its London office in 2016, and has more than 120 full-time employees on site, according to the company. According to Ripple, London is the company’s largest second headquarters outside of its head office in the United States.

The office capacity went from two full floors with a lot of unused space in 2018 to a 3rd floor that is now full, said Craddock. That growth comes alongside a broader regulatory push in the UK. In September 2026, FCA launched its new, crypto-smartened authorization gateway even though the new regime kicks in Oct. 25, 2027.

Read More: Ripple Expands BNY Deal to Bring $2.5B RLUSD and XRP Into Trade Finance

Ripple Secures UK Regulatory Permissions

In January 2026, the FCA granted Ripple an Electronic Money Institution licence and a registration for cryptoassets. The permissions enable the company to extend Ripple Payments to UK institutions, such as cross-border payments service using digital assets.

For Ripple, it means it has now gained regulatory clarity to do business with banks, asset managers and other regulated financial institutions in the UK.

£22B Aviva Fund Moves Onto XRP Ledger

The current embodiment is the strongest in recent years: Aviva Investors. Aviva on Oct. 26 launched a tokenized share class on its Sterling Liquidity Fund on the XRP Ledger. Its underlying fund holds a value of approximately £22 billion which represents Aviva Investors largest fund.

The tokenized share class will have a structure that is referred to as a “digital twin”, which is where the onchain share is still connected to, and not part of, the current fund structure.

The investor has the same objective, risk tolerance, liquidity and regulatory features as in the traditional version. The Aviva tokenized Sterling fund had cost £50 million to set up and assets in its two tokenised share classes topped over £86m.

XRPL Gains Another Institutional Tokenization Use Case

The Sterling fund is Aviva’s second liquidity token on XRPL. Its initial share class tokenisation offering debuted in July 2026 as a result of the announced partnership with Ripple in February.

Eligible investors with digital wallets can buy the new version of Sterling, which are known as underlying assets and remain with custodian BNY.

On the other hand, for Ripple the transaction is part of a broader institutional adoption of XRPL through the issuance and management of tokenized fund interests on the public blockchain infrastructure.

title: Privacy Cash Freezes Deposits After $1.2M Binance Hack Funds Hit Its Privacy Pools
summary:
Key Takeaways: Privacy Cash has temporarily suspended all deposits. Investigators mapped the fate of around $1.2 million in stolen ETH and SOL for their privacy pools. Redrawals are kept active
The post Privacy Cash Freezes Deposits After $1.2M Binance Hack Funds Hit Its Privacy Pools appeared first...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Privacy Cash has temporarily suspended all deposits.
  • Investigators mapped the fate of around $1.2 million in stolen ETH and SOL for their privacy pools.
  • Redrawals are kept active until the protocol’s wallet-screener enhancements are released.

Wallets connected to the Binance hack have been sending cryptos through Privy’s privacy layers, prompting the service to temporarily halt new deposits.

It also confirmed the suspension will be used to prevent illegal users from transacting on the platform while improving wallet screening and noted that withdrawals will be proceeding during it.

Read More: Binance Hacker Sends $798K in SOL to Privacy Cash, Laundering Spreads Across 11 Chains

  • Privacy Cash Suspends New Deposits
  • Binance-Linked Crypto Reaches Privacy Pools
    • Mixers Become Part of a Larger Laundering Strategy
    • Billions in Binance Funds Remain Traceable

Privacy Cash Suspends New Deposits

Privacy Cash said the decision was directly linked to the recent Binance breach. The project declaration emphasized that its purpose is to offer financial privacy for regular users, and not infrastructure for laundering stolen assets. It didn’t give any timeline on when the deposits would reopen.

We’re pausing Privacy Cash deposits temporarily.

When we started Privacy Cash, our goal was to make privacy tools for everyday people, not to enable crime. In light of the recent Binance hack, we want to make sure bad actors can’t use our product.

During the pause, we’ll continue strengthening our wallet screening system.

Withdrawals will remain available.

Stay tuned for updates on when the service will resume.

Thanks for understanding. Privacy is for everyone, but not for criminals.

— Privacy Cash (@theprivacycash) November 4, 2026

During the lull, the team pledged to enhance the screening processes that could detect suspicious wallets before the money lands in its pools. None of the withdrawals is impacted, so existing users of Privacy Cash can still withdraw their funds, and new deposits will not be accepted.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

Binance-Linked Crypto Reaches Privacy Pools

The pause comes after a significant ramp-up of laundering just tied to the Binance-heist that cost them $6.43 billion. The attackers have been shifting money between cryptowallets, decentralized exchanges, cross-chain bridges, lending platforms and mixers on 11 different blockchains, Elliptic said. In the first few days of the operation, about 12,000 wallets and over 40,000 transactions have been utilized.

Elliptic tracked ETH and SOL with this theft and detected them moving into Privacy Cash. Then more deposits onto Solana were spotted, bringing the combined total value to roughly $1.2 million and further complicating an already well-established and splintered laundering network.

Mixers Become Part of a Larger Laundering Strategy

One such path being taken is Privacy Cash. Elliptic has been able to track stolen money since the cross-chain bridges, DEXs, pooling strategies, and Bitcoin mixing dynamics. However, some batches traversed many blockchains in hours, making tracing of transactions more complex, the firm said.

The laundry also is heavily automated. The community is active, even some patterns of repetitive transactions were seen occurring almost continuously and Elliptic timed transactions as a set. The peak of laundering transactions on Tron was around 1,300 transactions in an hour.

Billions in Binance Funds Remain Traceable

Despite the cross-chain movement and mixing, most of the crypto has yet to be cashed out.

About $2.85 billion has been frozen or seized, and billions more remain in addresses associated with the attack, Elliptic estimates. The crypto firm also released its free blocklist allowing exchanges and crypto companies to filter funds for exposure.

But that leaves centralized exchanges, OTC brokers and other points of cashing out as major choke points for investigators.

It’s a pressure that is not limited to exchanges, and is now also hitting the privacy protocols, as Privacy Cash suspended deposits.

title: Binance Replenishes 98% of $6.34B Hack Losses, Expands Proof of Reserves to 44 Tokens
summary:
Key Takeaways: According to Binance, the company has replaced approximately 98% of the assets that were stolen in the $6.34 billion hack operation. The exchange now increased its new Proof
The post Binance Replenishes 98% of $6.34B Hack Losses, Expands Proof of Reserves to 44 Tokens appeared first o...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • According to Binance, the company has replaced approximately 98% of the assets that were stolen in the $6.34 billion hack operation.
  • The exchange now increased its new Proof of Reserves snapshot from 10 to 44 tokens.
  • The other 2% requires a longer amount of time to replace as the assets are less liquid.

Binance has been making additional progress in covering the funds impacted by the massive security assault on their exchange, buying the rest of its tokens from both the marketplace and their OTC channel.

Meanwhile, the exchange has aggressively grown its Proof of Reserves coverage, providing increased transparency for its users.

  • Binance Replenishes 98% of Impacted Assets
  • Recovery Moves Beyond the Largest Tokens
    • Proof of Reserves Expands From 10 to 44 Tokens
    • Binance Pushes Transparency After the Hack

Binance Replenishes 98% of Impacted Assets

Binance said approximately 98% of the affected amount has now been replenished, up from the 95% level disclosed in an earlier recovery update. The company has allocated a surplus of over 100% of its resources to the call for funding losses and claims that users will not be affected financially by the incident.

The other 2% is a little bit more difficult to replace because those tokens are not that liquid. Binance stated it will continue to purchase the assets from the public market and OTC platforms. Some of the balances that have been affected will be restored but replenishment may be longer as it is now in the last mile.

Read More: Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B

Recovery Moves Beyond the Largest Tokens

These more liquid assets were all accounted for in a prior post: 95% Milestone published earlier. The rest of the liquidity is believed to be swapping tokens that are not among the top five crypto assets by market value, and conducting large trades may require more effort.

The exchange is also gradually reinstating withdrawals, as it further tightens security measures.

Proof of Reserves Expands From 10 to 44 Tokens

Binance made a fresh snapshot of its Proof of Reserves on Nov. 4 at 00:00 UTC. There are 44 tokens included in the snapshot, versus only 10 in the previous reserve snapshot check post-incident.

The PoR system at Binance references a Merkle Tree structure and makes use of the zk-SNARK technology to enable buyers to confirm that they held a stability in the reserve snapshot without revealing specific account balances.

The exchange faces the computational heft, with the full ZKP mechanism to come up with the new snapshot taking roughly 50 to 60 hours. When complete, all users with any of the 44 supported tokens can verify their safety on their own through the ratio of backing of at least 1:1.

Binance Pushes Transparency After the Hack

The extended reserve snapshot provides a wider coverage of the time when Binance had a big problem.

While proof of reserves is not enough to ensure that an exchange is free of security events, it does establish a cryptographic assurance that funds in the covered accounts have equal balances in reserve assets.

Binance said it will keep acquiring the remaining tokens, restore more withdrawal services and publish further recovery updates as the process continues.

title: XRP Price Prediction: Whale Wallets Hit 2026 High as Elliott Wave Setup Points to $2 Rally
summary: XRP whale accumulation has reached a new 2026 high despite recent price weakness, while bullish Elliott Wave projections place $2 within reach if key resistance levels give way.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

XRP whale accumulation has reached a new 2026 high despite recent price weakness, while bullish Elliott Wave projections place $2 within reach if key resistance levels give way.

Santiment data shows that wallets holding at least 1 million XRP have climbed to 2,147, suggesting increased accumulation among large holders. At the same time, technical analysts are identifying potential reversal signals around $1.30, with Fibonacci extensions pointing toward higher price targets. However, XRP still faces resistance around $1.33–$1.56, leaving confirmation of a sustained recovery dependent on further buying pressure.

XRP Whale Wallets Reach Highest Level of 2026

On-chain data provider Santiment reports that the number of XRP wallets holding at least 1 million tokens has increased to 2,147, marking the highest reading so far in 2026. The count has added 28 wallets over the past 10 days, including 18 in the most recent three-day period. The increase comes as XRP trades under pressure near $1.30, highlighting a difference between large-holder activity and broader price performance.

XRP’s million-token holder wallets reached a 2026 high of 2,147, increasing by 28 over the past 10 days. Source: @SantimentData via X

The growing wallet count suggests that some large investors are accumulating XRP rather than reducing their exposure during the recent pullback. Santiment’s chart shows the number of millionaire wallets climbing toward a yearly peak even as XRP’s price candles reflect considerable volatility. This divergence has attracted attention because sustained accumulation during market weakness can indicate confidence among larger holders. However, wallet counts alone cannot establish whether every increase represents fresh buying, as transfers between addresses can also affect the figures.

The $1.20–$1.25 region remains an important reference area for monitoring this trend. If XRP maintains support around these levels while millionaire wallet numbers remain elevated, the on-chain picture could provide a constructive signal for longer-term market sentiment. Conversely, a decline in large-holder activity alongside a breakdown below support would weaken the accumulation narrative.

XRP 12-Hour Chart Shows a Potential Buy Signal

Technical analyst Jesse Olson (@JesseOlson) has identified a potential buy signal on XRP’s 12-hour Binance chart after the cryptocurrency found support at a horizontal level he described as a “sniper target.” His chart marks the support reaction with an upward arrow and highlights an attempt to break above a descending trendline.

XRP’s 12-hour Binance chart shows price bouncing from a key sniper-target support level while attempting to break its descending trendline. Source: Jesse Olson via X

The setup suggests that buyers are attempting to regain control after a period of downward price movement. Olson’s analysis also raises the possibility of a confirming buy signal on the daily timeframe, which would provide another indication that selling pressure is easing. XRP traded around $1.30–$1.31 during the early November session, recording gains of more than 2% over the day.

Olson, who operates MarketSniperPro, focuses on identifying specific support and resistance areas for cryptocurrency swing trades. His 12-hour chart signal remains an early technical indication rather than confirmation of a broader trend reversal. A sustained move above the descending trendline, followed by a stronger daily signal, would provide additional evidence that XRP could extend its recovery.

Elliott Wave Analysis Points to a Potential $2 XRP Rally

An Elliott Wave analysis published by Intuit identifies a potential completion of XRP’s corrective B-wave, opening the possibility of an upward move toward $2. The analysis highlights a relationship between the duration and retracement of the first two corrective waves, with wave B lasting approximately as long as wave A and retracing 61.8% of its previous decline.

XRP’s Wave-B matches Wave-A in duration and retraces exactly 61.8%, with a potential internal double zigzag structure and strong bullish divergences across multiple timeframes. Source: Intuit on TradingView

The analyst also identifies a possible double-zigzag structure within wave B and bullish divergences across multiple timeframes. These conditions form the basis of a bullish interpretation in which XRP could begin another upward phase after completing its correction.

“From here, I suspect we begin a climb towards $2 over the next month,” Intuit wrote, outlining the expected direction of the next move. The analysis also identifies $1.20 as an important invalidation level. A break below that price would require a reassessment of the current Elliott Wave count rather than support the existing bullish projection.

XRP could be entering a major Elliott Wave 3 advance, with RSI turning higher and a break above $1.56 needed for Ichimoku-based confirmation. Source: Carolina via X

Another technical outlook from @Carolinatcwnl identifies the possibility of a new Elliott Wave 3 advance. The analysis points to an upward turn in the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and identifies $1.56 as a critical breakout threshold. A move above this level, supported by confirmation from the Ichimoku Cloud, could strengthen the bullish interpretation.

The accompanying Fibonacci projections identify $1.8815 as the 161.8% extension and $2.9032 as the 200% extension. These levels represent potential upside objectives if XRP establishes a sustained upward trend. However, they remain conditional projections rather than confirmed price targets, particularly while the cryptocurrency trades near $1.31.

XRP Price Forecast: Technical Indicators Show Mixed Signals

The broader technical picture presents a more cautious outlook despite improving short-term price action. XRP/USD recently traded around $1.30546 on Bitstamp, gaining approximately 2.37% during the latest session covered by the market readings. However, the aggregated technical summary remains neutral, with nine sell signals, nine neutral readings, and eight buy signals.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The 14-period RSI stands at 48.22, indicating that XRP is neither overbought nor oversold. The Average Directional Index (ADX) reads 18.06, suggesting limited trend strength. Meanwhile, the Stochastic oscillator remains neutral at 58.27, while the MACD carries a buy signal despite remaining below zero. These readings indicate some improvement in momentum but do not yet establish a decisive bullish trend.

Shorter-term moving averages offer some support. The 10-period and 20-period exponential moving averages (EMAs) stand at $1.28439 and $1.30177, respectively, both carrying buy signals. Their simple moving average counterparts also indicate buying pressure. The Volume Weighted Moving Average (VWMA) at $1.29468 and the Hull Moving Average at $1.29406 provide additional short-term support references.

However, intermediate and longer-term averages remain less favorable. The 30-period EMA stands at $1.31964, while the 50-period EMA is near $1.33379, both carrying sell signals. The 200-period EMA is also higher at $1.36196. This arrangement shows that XRP has recovered above several shorter-term averages but still faces overhead resistance from longer-period indicators.

The Relative Strength Index and low ADX reading also suggest that the current recovery lacks strong directional momentum. A sustained move above the $1.33–$1.34 region would therefore be an important development for buyers.

Looking Ahead: Can Bulls Push Toward $2?

The immediate technical outlook depends on whether XRP can maintain its recovery above the $1.29–$1.30 area and overcome resistance around $1.33–$1.34. The classic pivot level stands at $1.33398, making it an important near-term reference. A decisive move above this area could bring the next resistance levels at $1.40197 and $1.46997 into focus.

Further gains could expose the Fibonacci pivot resistance near $1.55429, which also aligns with the $1.56 breakout threshold identified in the Elliott Wave analysis. Clearing this area would strengthen the case for a move toward $1.8815, the first significant Fibonacci extension target. A continuation of the rally could then put the $2 psychological level within reach, broadly aligning with Intuit’s projection.

On the downside, the $1.2939–$1.2133 region represents an important nearby support zone. The 200-period simple moving average near $1.27282 also provides a reference for assessing whether buyers can defend the recent recovery. A sustained move below $1.20 would weaken the bullish Elliott Wave structure and require a fresh assessment of the price outlook.

Overall, XRP’s latest on-chain and technical developments present a potentially constructive setup, but they do not yet confirm a sustained trend reversal. The increase to 2,147 millionaire wallets provides evidence of growing large-holder participation, while the 12-hour buy signal and Elliott Wave projections offer possible upside scenarios. For the $2 target to become more credible, XRP would need to reclaim successive resistance levels, particularly $1.56, while maintaining support above $1.20. Until those conditions are met, the market remains in a transitional phase between accumulation signals and an unconfirmed recovery.

title: Gold Price Forecast Faces December Fed Test as $3,900 Support Comes Into View
summary: As gold prices retreat from $4,000, the safety index is coming.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAU

As gold prices retreat from $4,000, the safety index is coming.

The December Fed decision could be the turning point for bullion to rally or continue its drop at the end of the year, with sellers pushing toward $3,900 support.

Gold Price Analysis Shows Sellers Still Control the Trend

Gold is struggling to be bullish in November trading below a key area near the $4,000 mark. Investing.com’s November 3 chart showed gold futures at $3,946.85, down $22.75, or 0.57%. Meanwhile, the TradingView chart shows spot gold trading at $3,935.13 on the current four-hour candle, down 0.24%. These are independent instruments, and their prices ought not to be compared.

Gold has been chopping around a bit in the $4600 range since its August recovery, with a series of lower highs and lower lows on the four-hour chart. Source: TradingView

The sales pressure then drove prices back to $3,900. The liquidity heatmap shows a cluster of potential resistance at around 4,200-4,600 and a large liquidity zone around 3,800-3,900. These zones are used to show zones that traders can watch for, not certain turning points.

In the near term, 3,900–3,880 is the key support area. A break below will open $3,800 and possibly the $3,700s. But gold has to clear 3,975-4,000 before bulls can put up a fight at $4,044 and begin the recovery. Any move above these areas would be a positive development technically, but the overall downtrend would need to be confirmed.

December Fed Decision Could Determine Gold’s Direction

The Fed kept interest rates steady at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28, with two members wanting to raise rates by a quarter point. The Fed also indicated that inflation continues to be high. The disagreement puts investors on edge about the possibility of a further contraction by policymakers at the Dec. 8-9 meeting. Read the official Fed statement and 2026 meeting calendar.

A rate increase or hawkish sentiment may extend the downward trend for gold as it helps to lift Treasury yields and the US dollar. The larger the crop, the greater the opportunity cost of carrying non-yielding bullion.

But if the inflation report is less severe and the employment report comes in light, or the Fed outlook is less hawkish, then rate expectations will be lowered, bringing gold back. Investors will need to monitor upcoming U.S. inflation and jobs data, as well as the dollar and real yields, rather than rely on the Fed’s decision to move prices.

Can Gold Rally in November and December?

There is still a chance that it will be able to make a decent rally, but the charts do not confirm one just yet. Gold must drink this resistance at 3,880–3,900; if it can cut through, it will recover $4,000 and break through on and off the resistance levels. In November, if those conditions persist and yields continue to drop, MBLIO investment demand could increase; a $4,044 or higher resistance may emerge. Lack of support to be found would instead continue the bear case for December.

Central-bank demand could be a source of demand in the longer term, and geopolitical risks could drive safe-haven buying. However, neither of these is a sure sign of recovery. Rather than just buying when gold has dropped significantly, investors should think about entering gradually, setting positions, and predetermined exit points.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. What’s the important price level for gold?

The immediate support zone is 3,900–3,880. If it falls below and continues to do so, $3,800 will be left vulnerable.

2. Will $4,000 be the minimum price for gold by November?

Yes, if the buyer supports and recovers $4,000. The recovery must be confirmed above $4,044 to support a stronger recovery.

3. What is the likely impact of the Fed on gold in December?

Hawkish policy sentiment and higher rates could weigh on gold, while dovish policy sentiment and lower yields could work in favor of gold.

4. Should you invest in gold now?

It is dependent on risk-taking capability and investment time horizon. It is better to be prudent rather than assuming a bottom, as it is currently in a downtrend.

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Binance hacker wallet deposited 8,567 SOL, or approximately $798,000, to Privacy Cash.
  • Elliptic mapped the laundering chain over approximately 12,000 wallets and 11 blockchains.
  • Approximately $3.18 billion of stolen crypto is in addresses related to the attack.

The laundering process is rapidly evolving for activities linked to Binance’s massive hack on Solana, with the stolen tokens now traveling through a privacy-focused mixer. Onchain Lens said a hacker-linked address deposited 8,567 SOL, valued at roughly $798,000, into Privacy Cash, while other related wallets showed similar activity.

BINANCE HACKER STARTS USING MIXER TO LAUNDER STOLEN FUNDS, MIXED 800K SO FAR ⚠️

An address linked to the hacker deposited 8,567 $SOL (~$798K) into Privacy Cash.

Multiple other addresses are showing similar activity. We are monitoring these movements in real time and working to trace and reconcile the full flow of funds.

@binance

— Onchain Lens (@OnchainLens) November 3, 2026

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

  • Binance Hacker Adds Privacy Cash to Laundering Route
  • SOL Is Being Split, Routed and Converted Into Bitcoin
    • Laundering Network Already Spans Thousands of Wallets
    • $3.18B in Stolen Crypto Still Remains Onchain

Binance Hacker Adds Privacy Cash to Laundering Route

The thefts of assets in Binance’s October 29 hack continue, with the Privacy Cash transfers as another development. Onchain Lens claims to be tracking the activity on stream and the work it is trying to connect the dots on the flow of funds.

Cross-chain moves in Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Bitcoin and other chains have occurred over the past few days for the SOL movement. In its first three and a half days, Elliptic estimates laundering was conducted on approximately 12,000 wallets on 11 blockchains, resulting in over 40,000 transactions.

Read More: Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B

SOL Is Being Split, Routed and Converted Into Bitcoin

Solana has become one of the active laundering routes. By November 3, about 87,000 SOL, worth roughly $8 million, had left the original theft wallet, according to Elliptic. This money was spread out for new addresses, turned into lending vaults and a liquid-staking service after which it was offered or exchanged for Bitcoin.

There was then a total of approximately 825,000 SOL in those addresses, the majority being held in two. The new entry into Privacy Cash seems to be a ploy to strengthen the embezzlement of funds while obscuring the obvious connection between incoming and outgoing transactions.

Laundering Network Already Spans Thousands of Wallets

Most beginning washing was done via Tron. The stolen TRX was spread out among roughly 7,700 TRX addresses and parts of its value were converted into Ethereum. Through various cross-chain bridges, at least $147 million has been withdrawn from Tron so far.

The aggressor has also switched both the assets and the networks by leveraging decentralized exchanges, lending platforms, and cross-chain swap services many times. The mixing of bitcoins started on the 1st of November. By early November 2, approximately 28 BTC worth of approximately $2.2 million went through a total of 18 CoinJoin transactions of WabiSabi variety.

The activity conveys the impression of being very automated, features set transaction patterns, amounts and the speed of wallet generation, Elliptic said. The quick operation resulted in approximately 32,000 transactions on Tron, the highest of which occurred at 1300 transactions per hour.

$3.18B in Stolen Crypto Still Remains Onchain

Regardless of the amount of laundering, the bulk of the stolen crypto isn’t out of the vault yet. As of Nov. 3, Elliptic estimated that $3.18 billion was left in theft-connected addresses, most of it in ETH and BTC. An additional $2.85 billion was already frozen or seized.

So far only minimal amounts have been on to a cash-out channel, the firm said. That means centralized exchanges and OTC brokers are essential places to catch and freeze.

PANAMA CITY, November 4, 2026 — Bitbase today launched ORIGIN, the first season of its Bitbase Points program, which is designed to reward sustained participation over time. Over the 26-week season, which ends on May 4, 2027, Bitbase will distribute 1,000,000 points each week, allocated daily according to each participant’s contribution.

Four sources of contribution

Each participant’s contribution is drawn from four sources: trading, assets held on Bitbase, consistent activity and referrals. Consistent activity is counted as a separate source, so continued participation from day to day adds to a user’s contribution. All eligible users, whether new to Bitbase or already active on the platform, are enrolled automatically.

For each new user referred directly, the referrer receives an additional 25% of that user’s contribution. The new user’s own points are not affected.

Participants will also receive a Trading Identity card, a shareable summary of their trading style. The first cards will be issued on November 9, with new cards following each Monday for the remainder of the season.

Existing users begin with points already credited

Before the season began, Bitbase credited points to eligible existing users based on their earlier activity on the platform. As a result, these users enter ORIGIN with their prior activity already reflected in their points and ranking.

The first program under Bitbase 2.0

On November 2, the exchange introduced Bitbase 2.0, updating its brand, app and website under the statement “Market Flows. We Focus.” ORIGIN is the first program to put that statement into practice. While markets move continuously, Bitbase has chosen to assess participation across months rather than individual moments.

“We designed ORIGIN for users who participate consistently, not only during the busiest periods in the market,” said Nicholas Lo, Chief Business Officer at Bitbase. “Over a six-month season, that consistency carries weight. Our responsibility is to make sure every contribution is credited, from the first day of the season to the last.”

Points and rankings are available in the Bitbase app and at bitbase.com/points.

About Bitbase

Bitbase is a digital asset exchange serving individual and institutional users worldwide, with products spanning Spot, Futures, TradFi and Earn. Bitbase aims to give users a stable and straightforward trading experience, in line with its brand statement, “Market Flows. We Focus.” Learn more at bitbase.com.

title: Bitbase launches ORIGIN, distributing 1M points every week

content:
Panama City, November 4, 2026 — Bitbase today launched ORIGIN, the first season of its new Bitbase Points program. Ahead of the launch, the digital asset exchange credited points to eligible users who had been trading on the platform, so their past activity counts from day one. The season runs for 26 weeks, until May 4, 2027, with 1,000,000 points distributed each week.

Part of Bitbase 2.0

ORIGIN is also the first part of Bitbase 2.0 to reach users directly. Bitbase unveiled 2.0 on November 2, with an upgraded app and website and a new brand identity built around the statement “Market Flows. We Focus.” The idea is that markets will always move, and Bitbase chooses to focus on what lasts for its users. ORIGIN applies the same thinking to participation. Rather than rewarding a single burst of activity, it looks at what users do day after day over six months and credits the contribution they make across that period.

How participation is counted

Bitbase built ORIGIN around what users already do on the exchange. Eligible users, new or existing, are enrolled automatically, with no separate registration. Points are allocated daily based on each participant’s contribution, which draws on four sources: trading, assets held on Bitbase, consistent activity and referrals. Because consistency is one of those sources, steady participation adds up over the course of the season.

ORIGIN also rewards users who bring others to Bitbase. A referrer receives an additional 25% of the contribution of each new user they refer directly, while the new user’s own contribution is unaffected.

Starting November 9, participants will also receive a shareable Trading Identity card that reflects their trading habits, with a new card issued every Monday until the season ends.

Recognition that continues through the season

“Bitbase 2.0 is about focus, and for our users, that means knowing their steady participation is recognized and credited,” said Nicholas Lo, Chief Business Officer at Bitbase. “That’s why ORIGIN started by crediting what users had already done with us. It doesn’t ask anyone to trade differently. It simply records the participation that’s already there, every day, for the next six months.”

Users can track their points and rankings in the Bitbase app and on the website. Full details are available at bitbase.com/points.

About Bitbase

title: Bitcoin Price Prediction: Can BTC Reclaim $80K as US Midterm Election 2026 Fears Fade?
summary: Bitcoin recovered above $78,000 on November 4 after an election-night decline below $76,000, leaving traders focused on whether renewed spot demand can sustain the rebound.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin recovered above $78,000 on November 4 after an election-night decline below $76,000, leaving traders focused on whether renewed spot demand can sustain the rebound.

The US midterm election results initially triggered another wave of selling, but BTC quickly recovered as political uncertainty eased. Spot buying pressure, moving-average support, and liquidation levels are now shaping the short-term Bitcoin price prediction, with $80,000 remaining an important upside threshold.

Bitcoin Price Today Rebounds as Election Uncertainty Fades

Bitcoin experienced sharp volatility as the 2026 US midterm election results emerged. BTC traded near $78,000 before losing ground as early results indicated a Democratic victory in both chambers of Congress. The selling accelerated overnight on November 3 and pushed the Bitcoin price to approximately $75,618 on Bitstamp, its lowest level in almost seven weeks.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

However, buyers quickly entered the market near the $76,000 region. Bitcoin subsequently recovered toward $78,000, reversing much of its election-related decline. Reuters reported that BTC reached approximately $78,354 on Wednesday, November 4, while Ethereum also recovered alongside other digital assets.

The initial reaction reflected concerns about potential changes to US cryptocurrency policy under a Democratic-controlled Congress. However, market participants had already anticipated much of the election outcome, limiting the possibility of prolonged selling once the results became clearer.

Kelly Ye, head of research at Talos, highlighted this positioning in comments to Cointelegraph. She noted that Bitcoin’s post-election movement was close to what options markets had anticipated, adding that “the election was the main event, but markets had largely prepared for it.”

The recovery suggests that traders are beginning to shift their attention from election-related uncertainty toward technical levels and underlying demand. Nevertheless, reclaiming $80,000 would require additional buying pressure rather than simply reversing the latest decline.

Bitcoin Spot Buying Pressure Contrasts With Futures Selling

Trading activity across spot and derivatives markets is offering another indication of Bitcoin’s short-term direction. Crypto trader Ted Pillows shared a 15-minute BTC chart on November 4 showing positive spot cumulative volume delta (CVD) of approximately $218 million against negative futures CVD of around $482 million.

The analysis indicates limited further downside from the election outcome, with the chart showing a recovery following a sharp intraday decline. Source: Ted via X

CVD measures the difference between aggressive buying and selling activity over a selected period. Positive spot CVD indicates that market participants are placing more aggressive buy orders than sell orders in the spot market. Meanwhile, negative futures CVD reflects greater selling pressure across derivatives trading.

The divergence suggests that spot buyers are absorbing some of the selling activity generated in futures markets. This distinction is important because a recovery supported by actual spot purchases can have a different market structure from one driven primarily by leveraged positions.

Ted Pillows described the spot buying pressure as encouraging and argued that the Democratic election victory had largely been priced into the market. The accompanying chart showed Bitcoin recovering after an intraday decline, indicating that buyers were willing to enter at lower prices.

However, positive spot CVD does not guarantee a sustained reversal. The indicator reflects activity during a specific period and may change as market conditions evolve. Continued spot accumulation, accompanied by improving derivatives positioning, would provide stronger evidence that the recovery is gaining traction.

BTC Reclaims 100-Day Moving Average After Election Dip

Bitcoin’s daily chart is showing an important technical development following the election-related volatility. According to TradingShot’s TradingView analysis, BTC briefly dropped below its 100-day moving average before recovering rapidly after the election results.

BTC briefly fell below its daily MA100 but rebounded sharply, recovering all losses following the U.S. midterm election results. Source: TradingShot on TradingView 

This marked the first break below the daily 100-day moving average since August 19, when Bitcoin began a strong recovery from its previous bear-market bottom. The subsequent rebound has brought the technical indicator back into focus as traders assess whether the latest decline was a temporary breakdown or the beginning of a deeper correction.

The distinction between these scenarios will depend on Bitcoin’s ability to maintain its position above the moving average. A sustained hold could support further recovery and improve the medium-term price structure. Conversely, another decisive daily close below the indicator would weaken the bullish interpretation.

TradingShot also compared the latest price structure with a previous May decline. The analysis identified a similar 12.81% retracement toward the 100-day moving average, raising the possibility of another corrective phase if support fails.

If selling pressure returns, the 200-day moving average becomes an additional technical reference. TradingShot also highlighted the weekly 100-day moving average and the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement level as potential areas for buyers to defend.

These levels should be treated as technical reference points rather than guaranteed reversal zones. Bitcoin’s reaction around the daily 100-day moving average will provide further information about the strength of the current recovery.

Trader Realized Price Offers Another BTC Support Test

On-chain metrics are providing additional context for Bitcoin’s recent price movements. CryptoQuant highlights analyst TraderGemini’s report that BTC was trading close to its Trader On-chain Realized Price, an indicator measuring the average acquisition cost of coins that last moved between one and three months ago.

Bitcoin is testing its Trader Realized Price, which represents the average cost basis of coins last moved on-chain 1–3 months ago. Source: CryptoQuant via X

The metric provides an estimate of the cost basis for relatively recent market participants. When Bitcoin trades above this level, recent buyers generally remain in profit. This can encourage them to maintain their positions and potentially provide support during market corrections.

However, a sustained move below the Trader Realized Price could change investor behavior. Recent buyers may begin facing unrealized losses, increasing the possibility of selling pressure if the price fails to recover.

CryptoQuant’s historical chart shows that this cost-basis indicator has previously acted as support and resistance during different Bitcoin market cycles. Its current proximity to the BTC price therefore makes the level particularly relevant to the short-term outlook.

TraderGemini emphasized that holding this level and moving higher would indicate that the average cost basis of recent participants continues to support the market. A breakdown, followed by an unsuccessful recovery, could instead weaken the current bullish structure.

The indicator does not establish whether Bitcoin has reached a market bottom. Its value lies in showing how recent investors are positioned and whether their average acquisition price continues to attract buying interest.

$82K Liquidity Cluster Puts $80K Resistance in Focus

Bitcoin’s liquidation heatmap is highlighting another potential development for the coming sessions. Ted Pillows noted that BTC recently swept downside liquidity during its decline, leaving a concentrated cluster of leveraged positions around $82,000.

Bitcoin’s recent downside liquidity sweep has formed a large liquidity cluster near $82K, potentially attracting price higher and setting up a breakout attempt above $80K. Source: Ted via X

The CoinGlass heatmap covering October 21 to November 4 shows concentrations of leveraged liquidation levels across the $80,000–$85,000 region. These areas can attract the market’s attention because rapid price movements toward concentrated positions may trigger liquidations and increase trading activity.

With Bitcoin recovering from below $76,000, the $80,000 threshold represents the first important psychological and technical obstacle. A sustained move above this level could bring the higher liquidity concentration closer into focus, including the area around $82,000.

CoinDesk also highlighted the $80,000–$82,000 range as overhead resistance in its November 4 market analysis. Markus Thielen, founder of 10x Research, pointed to Bitcoin’s daily stochastic indicator, which suggested that the cryptocurrency had become oversold during the decline.

Thielen identified $82,000 as a potential recovery target based on the momentum reading. However, this remains an analyst’s technical assessment rather than confirmation that Bitcoin will reach that level.

Liquidation heatmaps also require careful interpretation. They estimate where leveraged positions may be concentrated, but these clusters can shift as traders open, close, or adjust their positions. They should not be treated as fixed price targets.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: Can BTC Reclaim $80K?

Bitcoin’s immediate outlook depends on whether buyers can maintain the recovery and overcome resistance around $80,000. The latest spot CVD reading, the rebound above the daily 100-day moving average, and the recovery from the election-night low provide several encouraging technical signals.

A sustained move above $78,000 would help strengthen the short-term recovery structure. If buying pressure continues, BTC could challenge $80,000 before testing the $81,900–$82,000 region. The latter area also aligns with the 50-day moving average near $81,911 in a contemporaneous November 4 technical assessment.

Nevertheless, the broader market structure remains vulnerable. Bitcoin’s recent decline showed that election-related headlines can quickly influence leveraged trading, while the presence of overhead selling pressure could restrict further gains.

On the downside, the $76,000 region remains an important area to monitor. Bitcoin’s election-night low near $75,618 and the 50-week moving average around $75,733 provide additional support references. A decisive breakdown below these levels could expose the longer-term 200-day moving average near $73,163.

Spot demand will also remain important. While Ted Pillows’ chart indicates that buyers have been active in the spot market, sustained recovery would benefit from continued accumulation and improving institutional investment flows.

CoinDesk reported that US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced approximately $515 million in outflows during October, followed by substantial withdrawals during the first two trading days of November. These figures suggest that institutional demand remains an important factor to watch as BTC attempts to regain higher price levels.

For now, Bitcoin’s recovery has reduced immediate election-related selling pressure, but it has not established a confirmed medium-term bullish reversal. Reclaiming $80,000 and maintaining support around the moving averages would provide stronger evidence of improving market conditions. Until then, the $76,000–$82,000 range remains an important area for monitoring the next phase of Bitcoin price action.

title: NEAR Mobile Hits #1 in Finance App Rankings and Charts Across 38 Countries as NEAR Ecosystem Gains Momentum
summary: Escaldes-Engordany, Andorra, 4th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Escaldes-Engordany, Andorra, 4th November 2026, Chainwire

Escaldes-Engordany, Andorra, November 4th, 2026, Chainwire

With over 1 million downloads, the NEAR ecosystem’s largest mobile wallet expands its global reach while launching gasless cross-chain swaps across 120+ assets and 35+ blockchains powered by NEAR Intents.

NEAR Mobile is gaining international traction, appearing in App Store rankings across 38 countries over a recent 31-day period, according to app ranking data from Toplify.

The self-custodial wallet reached #1 in Finance in Serbia, #2 in Hungary, and #4 in Moldova and Oman, highlighting its growing visibility across international markets. NEAR Mobile also recently reached #7 in Finance in Finland and Nigeria.

These milestones come amid growing attention around the NEAR ecosystem and its chain abstraction infrastructure. NEAR Intents, the protocol powering cross-chain execution across the ecosystem, has surpassed $33 billion in cumulative volume across 35 blockchains.

With more than one million downloads, NEAR Mobile is the largest mobile wallet in the NEAR ecosystem and continues to expand its capabilities with version 4.0.0, introducing a gasless experience designed to make blockchain interactions significantly simpler.

From Global Adoption to a Gasless Multichain Experience

As NEAR Mobile expands its international reach, its latest update addresses one of crypto’s biggest usability challenges: gas fees.

Traditionally, users interacting with multiple blockchains must maintain different native tokens to pay transaction fees, even when they already hold the assets they want to transfer or swap.

With version 4.0.0, NEAR Mobile sponsors relayer fees for supported transactions, enabling users to swap and move assets across supported networks without needing to hold NEAR or maintain native gas tokens across different blockchains.

Powered by NEAR Intents, NEAR Mobile provides access to more than 120 assets across 35+ blockchains, combining cross-chain execution, unified balances, staking and self-custodial asset management in a single mobile interface.

One Wallet. All Chains. Powered by NEAR.

Unified Balances Across 35+ Blockchains

Beyond removing gas complexity, NEAR Mobile addresses another major challenge in crypto: fragmented liquidity.

A user holding USDC across Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain and TRON traditionally has separate balances that may require manual bridging and network switching to use together.

Through NEAR Intents, NEAR Mobile can present supported liquidity from multiple networks as a unified balance, allowing users to send or swap aggregated assets without manually bridging funds first.

Cross-chain swaps can settle in seconds, bringing the experience closer to using a single financial account rather than navigating multiple independent blockchains.

By abstracting networks, bridges and gas tokens, NEAR Mobile makes NEAR’s chain abstraction technology accessible to everyday users.

The Largest Mobile Wallet in the NEAR Ecosystem

With over one million downloads and growing visibility across international Finance App Store rankings, NEAR Mobile has established itself as a leading consumer application within the NEAR ecosystem.

Available on both iOS and Android, the self-custodial NEAR wallet allows users to create and manage NEAR accounts, send and receive assets, stake NEAR and access multichain functionality directly from their phones.

NEAR Mobile supports onboarding through Google, Apple ID or email, combining a familiar mobile experience with self-custody and on-chain account recovery.

Experienced users can alternatively create or import wallets using a traditional mnemonic phrase.

The wallet also provides NEAR staking and access to NPRO staking, currently offering up to 8.58% APY.

As NEAR’s chain abstraction ecosystem continues expanding, NEAR Mobile aims to make its infrastructure accessible through an intuitive consumer-facing application.

NEAR Mobile at a Glance

  • 1M+ downloads
  • App Store rankings across 38 countries in a recent 31-day period
  • #1 Finance in Serbia, #2 Hungary, #4 Moldova and Oman
  • 120+ assets across 35+ blockchains
  • Gasless transactions for supported actions
  • Cross-chain swaps powered by NEAR Intents
  • Unified multichain balances
  • NEAR and NPRO staking
  • Google, Apple ID, email and mnemonic onboarding
  • On-chain account recovery and self-custody
  • Available on iOS and Android

About NEAR Mobile

NEAR Mobile is the largest self-custodial mobile wallet in the NEAR ecosystem, with more than 1 million downloads across iOS and Android.

Powered by NEAR Intents, the wallet enables users to manage NEAR, stake assets and access more than 120 tokens across 35+ blockchains through gasless cross-chain functionality and unified balances.

Its mission is to make NEAR’s chain abstraction infrastructure accessible to everyone by removing the complexity of networks, bridges and gas tokens.

One Wallet. All Chains. Powered by NEAR.

title: Solana Microscope Offers Open-Source Monitoring for Complex On-Chain Operations
summary: The Solana Foundation has described Microscope, an open-source monitoring approach for teams managing on-chain programmes and infrastructure.
content:
TL;DR: The Solana Foundation has described Microscope, an open-source monitoring approach for teams managing on-chain programmes and infrastructure. An alert is not a transaction blocker.

Operational tooling rarely generates the excitement of a new token launch, yet it can determine whether institutions trust a network enough to hold meaningful value on it. Teams want evidence that they can detect unexpected actions before the problem expands. Monitoring is one part of that process, not a substitute for preventive controls.

What the primary source establishes

The Solana Foundation has described Microscope, an open-source monitoring approach for teams managing on-chain programmes and infrastructure. The toolkit is designed to help operators inspect instructions, transactions and alerts while connecting observations to common monitoring workflows. It is an engineering tool, not an announcement that every Solana application now receives automatic protection against attacks. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

In a complex blockchain application, important activity can be hidden within technical transaction instructions that a general-purpose dashboard does not explain well. Monitoring tools try to decode those events and route relevant signals to people who can respond. This is useful for treasury movements, contract administration and unusual operational behaviour, but good alerts depend on choosing the right thresholds and maintaining the integrations.

Why this matters beyond the headline

The wider lesson is that on-chain transparency is not the same thing as operational comprehension. Transaction data may be public while a business still struggles to identify why an event matters or who should investigate it. A self-hostable tool can give teams more control over their monitoring stack, provided they manage uptime, access and alert delivery responsibly.

There is a meaningful gap between a fast transaction and a complete financial service. Solana infrastructure can settle digital assets, but an actual payments or securities product must also manage eligibility, legal rights, local currencies and exceptions. The best reporting follows the full workflow rather than assuming the chain’s speed is the entire product.

For additional perspective, it is worth reading our existing reporting on Solana’s Samsung Wallet rollout and user test and the latest Solana developer and payments coverage. They explain related market structure and should not be mistaken for evidence that every new proposal is already live.

What the announcement does not prove

An alert is not a transaction blocker. Microscope does not automatically fix a vulnerable programme, reverse an executed transfer or eliminate the need for security audits. False alarms can consume attention, while incomplete alert definitions can miss harmful activity. A monitored environment still requires tested incident procedures and clear accountability.

Distribution can be an advantage for blockchain applications, but the user experience needs to justify a change in behaviour. Developers also need monitoring and controls to support systems that operate continuously. A credible launch is one that describes available features, supported participants and how success will be measured after the initial announcement.

What to watch next

Watch for adoption in real applications, public documentation and integration examples showing how teams respond to alerts. The most useful evidence would involve measured detection speed and fewer unresolved incidents, rather than the number of dashboards deployed. For Solana developers, monitoring belongs alongside code review and permission design as a basic operating requirement.

title: SEC Updates Crypto-Asset FAQs as Firms Seek Clarity on Federal Securities Rules
summary: The SEC Division of Corporation Finance added questions 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 to its crypto-assets FAQ on November 2, 2026.
content:
TL;DR: The SEC Division of Corporation Finance added questions 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 to its crypto-assets FAQ on November 2, 2026. SEC staff positions may be informative without having the legal force of a statute, judicial judgment or final Commission rule.

This distinction is worth making because crypto regulation often arrives in several formats: speeches, staff statements, enforcement actions, proposals and final rules. They have different implications even when the subject is the same. A dated FAQ update merits attention without being promoted into a sweeping legal turning point.

What the primary source establishes

The SEC Division of Corporation Finance added questions 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 to its crypto-assets FAQ on November 2, 2026. The new staff answers address governance through foundations or organisations, what counts as control over participation and the difference between a functional network and a decentralised one. The page expressly says its answers represent staff views, have no legal force and have not been approved or disapproved by the Commission. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

A functioning crypto system can have a native asset that users need for programmatic activity without necessarily being decentralised. Under the staff explanation, decentralisation is a distinct question about whether any party or group holds operational, economic or voting control. A foundation or association involved in broad-based governance is not automatically a controlling central party; the actual powers and decision rules matter. This is a narrower, more useful clarification than saying every governance token has received a new legal classification.

Why this matters beyond the headline

The additions give lawyers and builders more concrete language for evaluating governance arrangements. A protocol may distribute votes widely while retaining privileged access, unilateral upgrade powers or concentrated economic influence. The staff view asks analysts to study those powers rather than rely on the mere existence of a formal foundation. That could influence how firms document their networks, although it does not eliminate case-by-case analysis or statutory legal requirements.

Crypto policy updates arrive as proposals, staff explanations, enforcement cases and final rules. Those documents carry different legal weight even when they use similar language. A careful article tells readers who issued the text, when it was published and whether it changes obligations now. That distinction is especially important for financial firms making compliance decisions.

This development also connects to two subjects our newsroom has been following: DTCC’s tokenization service and settlement controls and financial infrastructure and technology policy coverage. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

What the announcement does not prove

SEC staff positions may be informative without having the legal force of a statute, judicial judgment or final Commission rule. Investors should also resist the leap from regulatory discussion to token-price predictions. A frequently asked questions page is not an approval notice for any specific exchange, security or stablecoin.

Regulation ultimately affects operational choices: where customer assets are held, who can move them, how decisions are recorded and which risks are disclosed. The market can debate policy direction, but firms still need to map any published guidance to existing duties and the specific activity they carry out. General labels rarely answer those questions.

What to watch next

Watch for direct Commission statements, formal rulemaking notices, court decisions and clarifications that identify the affected transactions. Teams reviewing compliance can use the FAQ alongside primary legal sources, while documenting areas where further advice is necessary. Precision about who issued a document is essential to accurate policy reporting.

title: ECB Links Europe’s T+1 Securities Transition to a Broader Settlement Overhaul
summary: European Central Bank officials have discussed the planned move to T+1 securities settlement in October 2027 alongside longer-term work on tokenized…
content:
TL;DR: European Central Bank officials have discussed the planned move to T+1 securities settlement in October 2027 alongside longer-term work on tokenized settlement infrastructure. A future regulatory settlement date should not be confused with a finished network rollout.

The deadline matters most to firms that process transactions across several jurisdictions. They have to harmonise instructions, reconcile holdings and manage currencies while the clock gets shorter. Blockchain advocates should explain specifically which tasks become easier and which stay with regulated intermediaries.

What the primary source establishes

European Central Bank officials have discussed the planned move to T+1 securities settlement in October 2027 alongside longer-term work on tokenized settlement infrastructure. A speech published October 29 outlined how shortening the conventional settlement cycle and experimenting with new technology fit into wider financial-market modernisation. The two projects are related strategic topics, not a statement that blockchain technology will automatically replace Europe’s existing settlement systems next year. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

T+1 means most eligible securities trades settle one business day after the trade date, compared with a longer conventional cycle. Shorter cycles can reduce outstanding exposures and certain capital needs, but they compress the time available to resolve breaks, fund positions and coordinate across time zones. Tokenization addresses a different design question: how ownership records and money can move using new technical infrastructure.

Why this matters beyond the headline

The connection is operational discipline. A market trying to settle sooner needs robust automation, accurate records and predictable funding. Tokenized assets may eventually support more tightly connected workflows, but they are not necessary to achieve the near-term T+1 timetable. Existing post-trade institutions and banks still have crucial responsibilities.

A tokenized instrument must connect technical records with enforceable financial rights. Trading software can move a token quickly, but an issuer, custodian, transfer agent or settlement bank may still have to recognise the result. This is why tokenization announcements need to explain which part of the lifecycle is changing, not merely advertise that a blockchain is involved.

This development also connects to two subjects our newsroom has been following: DTCC’s tokenized securities infrastructure rollout and tokenized fund redemptions tested over a weekend. They explain related market structure and should not be mistaken for evidence that every new proposal is already live.

What the announcement does not prove

A future regulatory settlement date should not be confused with a finished network rollout. Different products and markets can have exclusions or distinct implementation rules. Nor should a policy speech be read as authorising every private tokenized security to circulate without existing investor-protection requirements.

Real settlement infrastructure is judged by whether it works on bad days, not just during presentations. Reconciliation, asset eligibility, funding, corporate actions and recovery from errors remain central. Continuous technical operation can improve coordination, yet it does not create market liquidity or remove the obligations of regulated participants.

What to watch next

Watch for detailed industry testing, bank funding arrangements and official updates on both T+1 readiness and central-bank-money experiments. The important measure is whether settlement failures and costs fall without shifting uncontrolled risk to participants. Europe’s timeline creates a concrete deadline, while the tokenization debate remains a longer-term architecture choice.

title: Coinbase Launches AI Agent Sign-Ups for Crypto Trading With Built-In Safety Limits
summary:
Key Takeaways: Coinbase has created a special page for AI agents to sign up. Actively search and trade crypto under AI tools under user-set limits. Every agent trades within Coinbase,
The post Coinbase Launches AI Agent Sign-Ups for Crypto Trading With Built-In Safety Limits appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Coinbase has created a special page for AI agents to sign up.
  • Actively search and trade crypto under AI tools under user-set limits.
  • Every agent trades within Coinbase, with separate portfolios and security measures.

Growing its platform more directly towards AI-driven trading, Coinbase has launched a new web page aimed at specifically registering software agents. CEO Brian Armstrong said the company wants Coinbase to become the “most AI-enabled financial account,” while the new Agents product lets users connect existing AI tools to their Coinbase accounts.

We added a new sign up page for Agents.

We’re building Coinbase to be the most AI-enabled financial account.

Give it a try: https://t.co/Vx3wBHQ0DT https://t.co/ObNGeBdX9T

— Brian Armstrong (@brian_armstrong) November 2, 2026

Read More: Coinbase Unveils AiFi After $100M in x402 Transactions, Targeting AI Agent Payments

  • Coinbase Opens Dedicated Access for AI Agents
  • Crypto Trading Moves Into Plain-Language Commands
    • Coinbase Adds Limits Around Automated Trading
    • USDC Payments Give Agents Access to Premium Data

Coinbase Opens Dedicated Access for AI Agents

The Coinbase for Agents page enables users to integrate AI assistants that support the agency and grant their access to the agency’s Coinbase accounts. The list of compatible tools means that tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Perplexity, Cursor, Hermes and Muse are all supported for use with Coinbase. Any agent that supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) can connect, but Coinbase also provides a command-line tool to connect for non-MCP agents.

After the connection, an agent can browse markets, examine one to in several situations make trades according to instructions from the account owner. Coinbase emphasises that the AI isn’t meant for Coinbase to make investment decisions for them. Rather, it follows instructions and permissions set by the user.

Read More: Coinbase Lists $2.6B RLUSD Across XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base

Crypto Trading Moves Into Plain-Language Commands

The major difference is that one can order trades without having to create a traditional trading bot in a programmatic language.

For instance, Coinbase provides examples like telling an agent to reprice a portfolio or make a recurring purchase of Bitcoin. More conditional instructions also are supported on the board, with reference to the market indicators.

Coinbase Adds Limits Around Automated Trading

Coinbase has put in place several controls on access by agents. Users can seek approval prior to trades, create a separate portfolio for their agent and can pull disconnection anytime. Coinbase also states effective 8 a.m. ET on Tuesday, agents were not allowed to transfer money out of exchanges.

All agents are subject to a limit imposed by Coinbase, thus minimizing the access of automated software to the accounts. The firm also notes that AI agents may make mistakes and the user is still in charge of agent actions and their trading choices.

USDC Payments Give Agents Access to Premium Data

AI agents are being paired with paid market data by Coinbase as well, with x402, an open payments standard for software agents.

Agent users in the US are able to access top-notch research and market data for purchase, without subscription or API key. Coinbase has set those limits at $5 per transaction and $50 a day at this point.

Unlike other platforms, there is no separate fee for Coinbase for agents, and trades by agents can be done with the same fees as the other Coinbase trades.
